items.statement: Component business grew 700-800% in FY24; expects multi-fold growth over next 2-3 years
items.quote: components, we have seen a significant growth of almost, let's say, 700-800% because the base was small. But component is something which is growing significantly. And going forward also we have a good order book for components.

items.statement: Aims to reduce RAC revenue dependence from 80-81% to below 70% in next 2-3 years
items.quote: we definitely aspire to bring down our overall dependence on the highest-selling product as we see down from 80% to, let's say, less than 70% in the next two to three years.

items.statement: AC average selling prices fell ~10% in FY24 vs FY23; upward movement started in FY25 due to copper price rise, impacting from Q2
items.quote: Compared to last -- actually compared to FY23 we already had a price fall in FY24. So just to add there has been almost a 10% roughly around 10% reduction in average selling price for ACs in FY24 as compared to FY23. Now, current financial FY25 we are seeing some upward movement which has started off late because of rise in certain commodities especially copper and others. So that is going to impa

items.statement: Q1 FY25 demand phenomenally strong due to overflow from Q4 FY24 and intense heatwave
items.quote: So in that terms if we see, Q1 is not just strong, it is phenomenally strong. And we see an upside of almost 50% plus in Q1 as compared on a Y-on-Y basis.

items.statement: Insourcing by brands settling down; same customers now sourcing more from EPACK
items.quote: a lot of insourcing, what we feared or what had impacted us in the last financial year FY24, we see most of it now settling down. And hence, there is an increase in demand from the same set of customers who had set up in-house capacities.

items.statement: Only Voltas expected to further expand in-house capacity by end of Q1 or beginning of Q2 FY25
items.quote: Based on the information available in public domain out of four or five known brands which had announced their plans to expand their capacities almost all have completed. So one larger brand Voltas is expected to enhance the capacities by end of this quarter or beginning of next quarter.

items.statement: Working capital days reduced from 91 days in FY23 to 45 days in FY24
items.quote: Furthermore, our efforts to optimize working capital management yielded promising results with a substantial reduction in working capital from 91 days in FY23 to 45 days in FY24.

items.statement: Debt to equity ratio reduced from 1.58x in FY23 to 0.37x in FY24
items.quote: Furthermore, our debt position has also reduced significantly resulting in reduction of debt to equity ratio from 1.58x in financial year 2023 to 0.37x in financial year 2024.

items.statement: PLI income of INR30 crores booked for FY24; INR15 crores received for FY23 in April 2024
items.quote: Further, we have booked an income of INR30 crores against P LI for FY24. So that's the income booked against PLI

items.statement: TLI benefit not yet availed; awaiting entitlement certificate for Bhiwadi facility
items.quote: With regards to TLI which is applicable to our Bhiwa di facility. So currently we have not availed any TLI benefit. We are still waiting for entitlement certificate which we hope will be available soon a nd once that is available we will have incentive against TLI from the Rajasthan government as well

items.statement: Management expects to outperform micro markets in FY25 driven by ARR growth and healthy occupancy, with incremental revenue from new ballroom and lease rentals, and positive margin influence from high ARR flow-through.
items.quote: So, you know, growth would be healthy . We would outperform the micro markets there and would be driven by ARRs and maintaining occupancy fairly healthy. So, that would be the kind of overall theme that we see playing in.

items.statement: Management targets adding 1,000+ keys over the next two years primarily through inorganic strategy, with 300 keys from Grand Hyatt Mumbai expansion and the balance from acquisitions.
items.quote: The aim is to add 1,000 plus keys over the next two years, primarily as I said, driven by inorganic strategy.

items.statement: Normative capex including refurbishment is ~INR 100 crores for FY25; significant capex for 300-key expansion atop Grand Hyatt Mumbai will occur in FY26 funded by internal accruals.
items.quote: So, CAPEX, we are talking about normative CAPEX, including refurb of INR 100 crores. So, it is not significant CAPEX. Most of it is already expended last year. And fresh CAPEX is going to be roughly INR 100 crores.

items.statement: Brownfield expansion of 300 keys atop Grand Hyatt Mumbai to start in FY26 and complete in 18 months by FY27.
items.quote: So, it will start by FY '26, and it should be complete by FY '27.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margins maintained at 45.4% (Juniper) and 35.5% (Chartered) in FY24; management expects margin expansion in FY25 driven by ARR flow-through and new revenue streams.
items.quote: On the margins, as I said, ARRs are a high flow through. So, that would be a positive influencer for our operating margins.

items.statement: ARR growth outperformed micro markets: Mumbai +9% vs market +5.5%, Delhi +22% vs market +14.6% (YTD March); airline crew rates increased ~48% in Delhi and Mumbai.
items.quote: For instance, Mumbai ARR grew 5.5% and this is not just the Comp-set, this is the broader market I am talking about. And we grew at above 9% in Mumbai year-to-date. And as far as Delhi is concerned, it was a 14.6% growth and for Juniper it was (+22%).

items.statement: Management sees $100 (Rs.8,500) ARR headroom to reach $250 minimum target from current ~$150 levels.
items.quote: Even with the ARRs the way they are, we're still at about $150 . Reasonably, the $250 is the minimum that we believe that we should be able to achieve. So , there is a still $100 headroom, which is about Rs.8,500 available to us.

items.statement: Demand expected to outstrip supply in luxury/upper upscale segments for considerable future; no significant supply increases expected in key markets (Mumbai, Delhi, Ahmedabad) for 2-5 years.
items.quote: No significant supply increases are expected in our markets. So, the demand will continue to outstrip the supplies , as also confirmed by many of the hotel sector experts.

items.statement: Grand Hyatt Mumbai refurbishment of 380 rooms by end-September 2024 to target transient guests; new 49,655 sq ft 'Showroom' banquet hall operational in FY25; second banquet hall in Ahmedabad by Q3 FY25.
items.quote: Four floors that is about 380 rooms will be refurbished and ready in operation by Q2 of 2024 which is basically in three months by September, 380 rooms will be fully refurbished for this transient high paying customer.

items.statement: Weekend MICE and social event strategy at Grand Hyatt Mumbai using two banquet halls to drive occupancy above 80-82% market taper levels.
items.quote: So, if you see what will happen is , we will be able to drive additional occupancy , additional room nights over the weekend, which will add to our occupancy rate.

items.statement: Delhi Aerocity development adding 6.3M sq ft retail/commercial by 2027; next hotels in Aerocity ~2 years out, providing clear runway for Juniper's Delhi asset.
items.quote: In recent publications we have read and we have come to know that the Delhi International Airport, that Aerocity is actually going to go through a further enhancement; 6.3 million square feet of space is being added by 2027.

items.statement: IPO raised INR 1,800 crores; INR 1,400 crores used for debt repayment by March 2024, remaining INR 100 crores underway to meet INR 1,500 crores IPO object; INR 330 crores in deposits for balance debt paydown and growth capital.
items.quote: We have raised INR 1,800 crores in the IPO, pure growth capital and we have utilized 1,400 crores as of March'24 to repay debt and significantly strengthen our balance sheet and the consequent ratios.

items.statement: Inorganic acquisitions may involve some debt but management commits to not exceeding 2-2.25x debt-to-EBITDA going forward.
items.quote: But at any point in time, going forward, we believe that we will not exceed debt-to-EBITDA of 2 to 2.25.

items.statement: Net bank debt-to-EBITDA reduced to 0.7x from 5.7x; INR 160 crores annual interest savings from debt paydown; JP Morgan NCDs replaced with ICICI loan at 2% lower rate (9%).
items.quote: Net bank debt-to-EBITDA going down to 0.7 from 5.7 x and a significant saving in interest cost which is INR 160 crores which will be as a result of the debt pay down that we have actually paid out.

items.statement: Room revenue ~48-49% of total, F&B ~30% (banqueting-driven); serviced apartments benefiting from FDI/expatriate demand in Delhi and Mumbai.
items.quote: The room revenue is 48%-49% and your F&B has been maintained at around 30%.

items.statement: Management expects revenue mix to shift to ~65% services, 30-35% training, 10-15% drone sales in FY25
items.quote: We think that it will start going in favor of services, more like 65% around that number it will go towards in services side. And the training would probably be around 30%-35%. And the drone sales is a new subject for us as well. We still think that it will add about 10%-15% of our overall revenue.

items.statement: Management targets maintaining ~40% EBITDA margin and ~20-22% PAT margin in foreseeable future
items.quote: We should continue to maintain, the EBITDA that we have seen, at least in the foreseeable future. That's what we think. That is about 40% right now, correct? That's about 40%. And PAT is about 20%. PAT is about 20%. 21%-22%, 20%.

items.statement: IFFCO order for 30 lakh acres of agri-spray to be completed by 30 September 2024
items.quote: The mandate of this collaborative approach in this memorandum agreement that we have signed is that let's try and achieve 30 lakh acres by that time.

items.statement: Industry indication of 9-10 crore acres agri-spray demand requiring 22,000-25,000 drones
items.quote: If the agri-sector picks up the momentum the way as of now it is envisaged, there is a likelihood of an order, this is what we learned recently, of at least INR 9 crores acres of Agri-Spray activity itself coming to the fold or into the market.

items.statement: Training capacity expanding from 6,000 to 10,000 students per year with INR 3-4 crore capex
items.quote: Our current capacity is of about 6,000 trainees a year, which we are expanding to 10,000 students this year.

items.statement: Capex of INR 3-4 crores planned to expand training capacity from 6,000 to 10,000 students
items.quote: So to kind of move from on an investment front, if we have to do, go from 6,000 to 10,000 capacity, we should be looking at an investment of about INR 3 crores to INR 4 crores.

items.statement: Plan to deploy 800 drones for agri-spray operations with 8-10 batteries per drone
items.quote: We intend to deploy at least 800 drones ourselves to cater to this demand that you have just mentioned of the order that we, of the activity that we are supposed to undertake.

items.statement: Agri-spray revenue per acre expected at INR 400-700 depending on geography, crop and timing
items.quote: So, the revenue expected out of an acre should be between INR 400 to about INR 700, depending upon the geography, crop, and the timing.

items.statement: Survey and mapping rates declared at INR 18,000 per sq km for Abadi area and INR 6,900 per sq km for large-scale mapping
items.quote: There are rates of INR 18,000 per square kilometer and INR 6,900 for large-scale mapping. This has been won by different companies.

items.statement: Drone sales operating margins expected at 15-18%
items.quote: The operating margins from these activities are likely to stay around 15%-18%.

items.statement: Trade receivable turnover improved from 3.49 to 2.48; private players pay in 2-3 months, training collected in advance or within 1 month, government projects have longer terms
items.quote: Our trade receivable turnover ratio has improved from 3.49 to 2.48.

items.statement: Outstanding receivables of INR 19 crores as of 31 March 2024 include recent second-half sales and advances for asset purchases
items.quote: Our outstanding of INR 19 crores includes our recent revenues mostly like we have done most of the sales. If you have seen our half yearly to half yearly results, most of our sales was done in the second half year.

items.statement: Company remains almost zero-debt
items.quote: We continue to be an almost zero-debt company.

items.statement: Preferential issue process ongoing; details to be disclosed after completion
items.quote: As of now, we are still in that process I must admit and we have already given a list of all the people who are coming in on our stock exchange listing.

items.statement: May consider technical acquisitions to accelerate growth but currently self-sufficient
items.quote: If need be in that specific scenario we may look at some technical acquisition to just fasten up the scale of growth. But at present, the company is pretty self-sufficient in terms of managing the current scale.

items.quote: Training has a 47% share in total revenue, agri services has 37% and drone sales have about 6% these are the major components of it. Survey and mapping is also 13% as of now.

items.statement: Drone soccer new revenue stream targeting <INR 5 crores in FY25
items.quote: As of now, in our business plan, you know we are keeping it very modest. We ar e still looking at less than INR 5 crores of rev enue coming out of drone

items.statement: Certified training market estimated at INR 45-50 crores; Drone Destination holds ~30% market share and 35% revenue share
items.quote: For FY23-24, Drone Destination has maintained roughly 30% market share and a 35% rev share of the certified training market estimated to be about INR 45 crores to INR 50 crores.

items.quote: Our average revenue this year has been rather decent. It is close to INR 65,000 in the last financial year. items.statement: Drone procurement from Hubblefly Technologies (15,000 annual capacity) and other OEMs; no manufacturing done in-house

items.quote: Whether the industry can deliver 25,000 drones this year. But if the industry can deliver that, then the training, there is a substantial training which is likely to happen, no doubt about that.

items.statement: Core management from aviation background; operating in 15 states with drone hub on wheels model
items.quote: The core management team comes from an extensive aviation background, which makes us very unique in this space. And that has, that's historically managed and successfully led some large-scale round-the-clock operations.

items.statement: Targets doubling seating capacity annually to reach 10,000 seats by FY26
items.quote: With this geographical diversification, we aim to actually double our seating capacity annually and we aim to reach 10,000 seats by FY '26 to meet the evolving needs of our clients and positioning ourselves for substantial growth.

items.quote: The capex per seat would be about, roughly about 80,000 to 90,000.

items.quote: So, in addition to our managed spaces, we are introducing a new managed office setup in one BKC itself. So, we already are running an existing center and we have taken up a new center in the same building.

items.quote: Not really. I think it would be maybe 5% to 7% lower.

items.quote: In fact, post the IPO, we've got some MNCs as well who have joined us, especially at the One BKC Center. items.quote: No. So we get into long-term lease-rental contract because that is in interest of the business. So anywhere to the north of five years and with a minimum lock-in of three years, that is the kind of agreement that we get into.

items.statement: Does not benchmark against WeWork; focuses on conservative, risk-averse growth with anchor-first strategy
items.quote: So Yashwanti, we -- for us, we like to set benchmarks what, where we are concerned, where we do better than what we did yesterday. Today we do better than what we did yesterday. I mean, it would not be fair for me to say XYZ is my competition or ABC is my competition because our positioning is very different.

items.statement: Total debt INR5 crores: one property loan for owned premise given to managed client, one vehicle loan ~INR60 lakhs
items.quote: Correct. So it's for a premise and for a vehicle. Jignesh Vayda: For a premise? Kanan Kapur: One of them is for our own -- one of the properties which we have given to the manager of this client, that is something which is owned by Kontor. And that is a loan that is there. And then there's a vehicle loan. That's about it

items.statement: FY25 expansion funded by IPO proceeds, internal accruals, and promoter capital; fit-out financing from NBFCs under discussion
items.quote: So we still have proceeds from the IPO. That is something that will go towards expansion. And then we're looking at internal accrues and the promoters will also put in more money into the company.

items.statement: Sales team ~12 people; finance/accounts/RTS ~6 people; zero salary hikes for management; headcount increased with senior sales hire and junior additions
items.quote: So we have a sales team of about 12 people. And we have a finance team, which has -- which includes accounts and finance and RTS, which is about six people. And then, of course, it starts in the management.

items.statement: Blended utilization target 85-90% across centres for FY25
items.quote: So I think blended utilization would be to the north of 85% across centers. I mean we are looking at 85% to 90% even going forward.

items.statement: New centre break-even occupancy at 60-65%
items.quote: So generally we breakeven at about 60%, 65%.

items.statement: Inter-corporate loan of INR4.92 crores to non-related party; will be recovered within FY25
items.quote: This definitely won't be in the FY 25 balance sheet.

items.statement: Exploring revenue-share model with landlords to reduce lease rental burden
items.quote: Definitely. As we speak we are in talks for this particular model.

items.statement: Geographical expansion targeting Bangalore, Hyderabad, NCR, Ahmedabad beyond Maharashtra
items.quote: Definitely we are looking at other micro markets in Mumbai. But at the same time, we're looking very aggressively in Hyderabad, Bangalore, NCR and also cities like Ahmedabad.

items.statement: Dubai subsidiary expected to be operational by Q2 or Q3 FY25; build-up year in FY25, material contribution from FY26
items.quote: we are incorporating this subsidiary and expecting it to be operational by Q2 or Q3 of this financial year. On number side, we expect this year will be a build-up year for Dubai subsidiary and from next year onwards it will start contributing material numbers on a consolidated level.

items.statement: Merger of Rockingdeals Private Limited expected to increase top line by 15-20% and bottom line margins by 1-2%
items.value: 15% to 20% top line, 1% or 2% bottom line
items.quote: Merger of Rockingdeals should help us to increase our margins at least by 1% or 2% on a bottom line level. And on a top line level also, once we consolidate, it will help us to increase the top line also by 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Ongoing investment of INR 2.5 crores for Guwahati warehouse facility
items.quote: our ongoing investment of about INR2.5 crores to establish a state-of-the-art facility in Guwahati reflects our dedication to growth and service expansion.

items.statement: Business model is working capital intensive, not capex intensive; capex only for new facilities
items.quote: Our business model is cash flow intensive not in terms of capex. Capex is only when we set up a new facility, but yes in order to buy more and more inventory it's working capital intensive.

items.statement: Guwahati warehouse expected to contribute 30-35% of overall turnover in FY25
items.quote: See, we think at least 30 % to 35% of my overall turnover in this year should come from Guwahati operations. Guwahati and Guwahati's extended operations.

items.statement: Three franchise stores operational in Northeast, one in pipeline; Guwahati warehouse to cut lead time
items.quote: See, we already have one, two, three. Three running stores in Northeast which are franchisee store and one in pipeline. Demand is very good there. That's why we decided first two years. items.statement: Growth driven by post-IPO brand additions, fashion category focus, and streamlined sourcing
items.quote: Our revenue composition more or less stays the same. We are focusing more on the fashion categories. And you have seen post IPO, we have signed with a lot of new brands as well. Post listing, we are able to add more and more new brands. And more sourcing, getting intact and streamlined, we will be able to do better numbers.

items.statement: Net profit margins around 11%; expect pressure on gross profit with volume growth but indirect costs won't rise as fast, hopeful to maintain net margins
items.quote: Our current margins are not 16% they are around 11% and as the volume will grow you can see some pressure on gross profit, but since indirect costs will not increase at that speed we are hopeful we will be able to maintain net profit margins.

items.statement: Retail channel gives highest margins; near-term margin uplift 1-2%, longer-term operating leverage from retail scale
items.quote: See, once we will add, for now, it will not be more than 1% or 2%, but in a longer term, it will be, you know, once a sizable number of stores and a sizable number of retail channels are there, then we get operating leverage and get a better, you know, boost to the bottom line. But for now, it will be a 1% or 2% increase in margins.

items.statement: Pricing benchmarked to online channels and brand factory outlets; must discount deeper than brand outlets (50-60% off)
items.quote: See, it's more like our pricing is decided one by what are the online channels they are selling at. We have to be cheaper than that. Second, what rate brand is selling if brand factory outlets are giving 50-off, 60-off. Generally, we have to discount more than that. So our margins are decided more like underlying pricing factor is at what rate brand new and or online is selling.

items.statement: Revenue mix dynamic based on sourcing; no fixed brand or category plans; currently 18+ categories but focusing on 2-3
items.quote: It's very dynamic because our industry is more around sourcing. So I'm more of a deal store, you know, where whatever I'm selling, it will be a very good deal. That's how

items.statement: Plan to first increase brands in few categories, then go deeper into categories
items.quote: Not really. First, we want to focus on a few categories and increase the number of brands. And then we will go deeper in the categories.

items.statement: Pipeline of 20+ brands for future tie-ups
items.quote: Yes, there is a pipeline of brands we are speaking to and there will be more and more brand tie-ups we will be doing in the future as well. We have more than 20 brands in the pipeline.

items.quote: Yes, they are our partners on sale or return basis. They are our SOR partners. They have supplied their inventory to us to be available to sell on our all channels, be it our B2B partners, be it our retail stores etc and on a monthly basis whatever throughput is we deduct our commission and pay them back.

items.statement: Inventory days 90-120 days (90 best, 120 worst)
items.quote: Currently it is somewhere between 90 days to 120 days. 120 days being worst and 90 days being best.

items.statement: Inventory write-offs less than 1%; garden sales events liquidate non-moving stock at 90% discounts
items.quote: Inventory write-offs are not much it's less than 1% because see my cost of buying is so optimized I can go as deep as 90% discounts as well. items.quote: Dubai subsidiary and from next year onwards it will start contributing material numbers on a consolidated level. items.quote: This year it is entirely B2B. Once our all operations are consolidated then we can look at a split for B2B and B2C.

items.statement: Target double-digit revenue growth with 20% EBITDA margin
items.quote: I'm happy to report that we are firmly on track to achieve our target of double-digit revenue growth with 20% margin.

items.quote: During the last year using the success of FCI HRMS solution, we were selected to do Karnataka state government HRMS platform that we are deploying, LIC has chosen us also to revamp their HR solution so the whole life of an employee is going to be taking care of us for more in the Karnataka state government, all the employees in the state government as well as the LIC.

items.statement: Product revenue from industrial IoT and hyper automation tools currently ~$0.5M; targeting $20-30M over 3-5 years
items.quote: We are probably in the half a million range of revenue. But we anticipate right over the next 3 to 5 years, 20 to 30 million revenues will be coming in from those.

items.statement: Headcount flat at ~1,800; hiring fluid based on demand with 20+ interns in Hyderabad being evaluated for conversion
items.quote: We are flat what we were last year. Ups and downs were there, there be some people left, but we were back to 1800.

items.statement: Revenue mix: 80% digital transformation, 7-8% SAP, balance consulting; Industry: ISV/Tech 30%, Health/Life Sciences 14%, Retail 12%, Energy/Utility 7.4%, BFSI 8.5%, Media 6.1%
items.quote: For us 80% of our revenue is from digital transformation, right, it is all digital is what we call. So that is the primary side of it. And then we have about close to 7% to 8% of SAP business and the balance is what we call the me-too.

items.statement: Most business comes from referrals; 40-60% from outreach/other channels; direct sales team handles RFP responses and field sales in US
items.quote: There is no concentration saying that okay, we get only from this, but most of our business comes from referrals.

items.statement: Premium pricing vs peers but faster delivery wins deals; competitive intensity high for new logos with 3-5 vendors typically
items.quote: So typically what happens there, Tushar, is our prices are higher, but what we are able to deliver is much faster than the others. So that is the reason why customers pick us because they can produce solution much faster sooner than others usually do.

items.statement: No significant internal R&D spend; AI use-case development done on customer projects and for sales enablement
items.quote: There is no real R&D as such right. We are using internally to see our efficiencies; we can build efficiencies into our own delivery kind of stuff. So, the R&D mostly is done on the job with the customer.

items.statement: Recovery dependent on US/UK election outcomes; slow growth expected for next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: We don't expect major recovery to happen until after the elections that take place in UK and US. So, we are looking at probably the next 2 to 3 quarters, it is going to be slow growth and then probably starting the next calendar year is when we'll start seeing the spending coming back as aggressively as what it is to be.

items.statement: FY25 volume guidance 110-115 million meters; EBITDA margin band 16-18%
items.quote: So that's why we have kept the band, as well as a band for both volume guidance and margin guidance.

items.statement: Branded business revenue target $100 million in next 3-4 years
items.quote: We are confident with the kind of product base and the customer base which we have, we should be able to have at least built up $100 million revenue in the next 3 to 4 years.

items.statement: Branded revenue share target 10-15% of total revenue
items.quote: So going forward, like say if we start with say 5% up to 10% and then maybe probably our endeavour is to go up to 15% of our revenue in the branded business.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 15% due to one-time promotional expenses impacting margin by ~2%
items.quote: EBITDA margin of 15% was on account of onetime promotional activities, which increased the other expenses and therefore, impacted EBITDA margin by around 2%.

items.statement: Branded segment EBITDA margin range 20-24%
items.quote: 20% to 24% should be considered.

items.statement: Branded products realizations 15-20% higher than commodity range
items.quote: See, normally, it is like what we've just now mentioned, it is around 15% to 20% higher than the normal range, because there are expenses to be considered.

items.statement: Wamsutta brand launch in September FY25; licensed brands Fieldcrest and Waverly active in FY26
items.quote: Brand Wamsutta, we'll be launching in this spring FY 2025 in this September. So we'll see some traction happening in the fourth quarter. And slowly, we will build up this brand. Also these brands -- licensed brands like Fieldcrest and Waverly also, they will become active in 2025. That is FY '26.

items.statement: Capacity expansion likely FY27, possibly FY26 if utilization reaches 85%
items.quote: That should be considered most like FY '27, I'd say, probably. But if we are lucky and if we are more successful, then definitely, we'll come forth in '26.

items.statement: Zero-liquid discharge effluent plant INR50 crores at Bhilad, Gujarat
items.quote: Yes,at Bhilad plant, because you see, as I mentioned, on the compliance side now, everybody is focusing on zero-liquid discharge. So we need to upgrade our unit. So we are investing into it.

items.statement: Cotton prices stable at INR60,000-62,000 per candy; expect similar band with good monsoon
items.quote: See, cotton prices, you see India is pretty strong in cultivation and producing cotton and that's the reason you see the cotton prices are more or less stable around the INR, 60,000 to INR62,000 mark.

items.statement: US sales >70% on FOB basis; target 60% US / 40% non-US long-term
items.quote: No, our overall mid to long -term strategy is to see that we have like a 60% -40% ratio, 60% in U.S. and 40% in non-U.S.

items.statement: UK FTA primary discussions completed; would provide level playing field vs Pakistan/Bangladesh
items.quote: What we hear is that the primary discussion has alre ady completed. And there are no hitches between the two government to declare the FTA. But they are taking their own time to declare it

items.statement: Maharashtra solar policy allows 4MW per meter; awaiting notification to expand Kolhapur plant from 1MW to 4MW
items.quote: Maharashtra, where we are located, do not have a sound solar policy because they allow only 1 megawatt on one meter. So recently, they increased in the textile policy to 4 megawatts. But still the notification is not out, according to which we can invest i nto it

items.statement: Inventory INR1,143 crores at March 31, 2024 aligned to service higher FY25 activity
items.quote: The inventory for year ended 31st March stood at INR1,143 crores. This should be looked at from the perspective of the increased guidance.

items.statement: Branded business working capital planned on made-to-order basis, not made-to-stock
items.quote: But that will be all planned on the made-to-order basis rather than on a made-to-stock basis.

items.statement: Dividend recommended INR2.20 per share (110%) for FY24; payout 12.89% kept stable for reinvestment
items.quote: The Board of Directors has recommended a higher dividend of INR2.20 per equity share of INR2 each. That is 110% subject to the approval of shareholders at ensuing AGM. The dividend payout stood at 12.89% and has been kept stable in order to use the cash for increased investment in business, especially the recent acquisition and inventory buildup.

items.statement: Value-added segments share improved from 46% to 51% YoY; 7 verticals beyond commodity sheets
items.quote: So we should look at holistically. I have predefined earlier that now we are working on almost 7 verticals apart from the sheet, which is a commodity. So we are working on fashion, utility, institutional, e-commerce, license brand and brand business as well as domestic.

items.statement: Wamsutta brand recall >75% in US; addresses 45+ age; Waverly 94% female recall; Fieldcrest targets 25+ age
items.quote: Wamsutta has a 45-years age and above brand rec all value, Waverly has got 94% feminic c recall value and it is more print and stylish driven as well as Fieldcrest is addressing more to younger generation, 25 years and above

items.statement: Pakistan gaining share due to cheaper MMF (25% cheaper than India) and freight advantage for filled products
items.quote: See, this is due to because Pakistan consumes MMF and in India MMF is expensive by almost 25% where China is cheaper. So India has so far not focused on the fi lled product

items.statement: Red Sea crisis increasing freight costs and working capital by 15 days; universal impact
items.quote: And secondly, one more important thing because U.S.A. is not impacted as such with this, because it goes with Cape of Good Hope, where only you are increasing the working capital by 15 days.

items.statement: India inflation >6% and geopolitical disruptions may delay revenue doubling target
items.quote: See, there are still geo-political reasons for business disruptions, the Red Sea, the war, like various inputs, which are increasing in India. The Indian inflation is like almost more than 6%.

items.statement: FY24 volume 96.8 million meters (+30% YoY); Q4 FY24 volume 28.7 million meters (+41% YoY)
items.quote: Sales volume for FY '24 stood at 96.8 million meters versus 74.7 million meters in FY '23, growth of 30%.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA INR603 crores (+24% YoY); margin 16.7% (+78 bps YoY)
items.quote: EBITDA for FY '24 stood at INR603 crores versus INR486 crores in FY '23, growth of 24%. EBITDA margin for FY '24 stood at 16.7% versus 16% in FY '23, growth of 78 bps.

items.statement: Pre-sales target of Rs 2,000 crore for FY25
items.quote: This year we have a target of Rs. 2,000 crores internally to get to , again it assumes that the market will remain buoyant the way it is , and we get to launch the phases as scheduled.

items.statement: Expects margin expansion with PAT margin reaching 17-18% gradually
items.quote: I think as the cycle keeps going, we probably get to after tax profit margins and the TCI margins closer to 17%-18% gradually as we go ahead.

items.statement: Targets 15% ROE by FY26 if deliveries go as planned
items.quote: Like FY’26, we will definitely hit 15% over ROE's if things go as per plan as per deliveries.

items.statement: Expects 25-26 lakh sq ft construction in FY25
items.quote: We do expect to do 25 -26 lakhs square foot of construction this year.

items.statement: Achieved highest ever sales value of Rs 1,798.22 crore in FY24
items.quote: We achieved a sales value of Rs. 1,798.22 crores for the financial year 2023-24 which is highest ever.

items.statement: Launched 10 projects totalling 23.19 lakh sq ft in FY24
items.quote: On operations, this year saw the launch of 10 projects, 4 Greenfield projects and 6 new phases of existing projects to the tune of 23.19 lakh s square foot.

items.statement: Expects gross profit margin expansion as construction cost as percentage of sales price to decline
items.quote: But as a percentage of sales price as I said, we are going to see gross profit margin expansion. And I think , as a percentage of sales price, construction cost to come down.

items.statement: Sales price improved 34% YoY to Rs 6,811 per sq ft in FY24
items.quote: Sales price improved to Rs. 6,811 for the year on a per square feet basis vis-à-vis Rs. 5,080 per square feet in the previous year, an increase of 34% on a year -on-year basis.

items.statement: Plans to launch Amarah Phase-4, 5 and Sector 80 project in Gurugram in FY25
items.quote: We have Ashiana Amarah Phase-4 and 5 to launch. We are hoping to launch it in this financial year both those phases and we have another project in Sector 80 in Gurugram which is not too far away from Ashiana Amarah. Also, we are hoping that we can launch that in the 4th Quarter of this year and if not 4th Quarter of this year , then the first quarter of the next year.

items.statement: Has 80-90 lakh sq ft launch pipeline excluding Milakpur land
items.quote: So, we have about 80-90 lakhs square foot to launch excluding Milakpur between our future phases and l and banks.

items.statement: Senior living target of 900-1,000 units/year in 3-4 years from 354 currently
items.quote: Right now, we are looking at from a medium-term view if we can get to about 900 -1,000 units a year from about 354 units a year today as compared to last year.

items.statement: Will not pursue hybrid projects; committed to full senior living projects
items.quote: don't think hybrid projects are the way to go. We don't think they create the value that a senior living consumer wants. Again, these are different opinions and different people can have different strategies. We want to do a full senior living projects wherever we want to go

items.statement: Recorded highest ever pre-tax operating cash flows of Rs 304.46 crore in FY24
items.quote: During the year, we recorded pre-tax operating cash flows of Rs. 304.46 crores which was the highest ever.

items.statement: Buybacks expected every 3-5 years depending on cash flow availability
items.quote: Buybacks will not happen every year. We hope that we do buybacks every 3-5 years depending on the cash flow availability of the

items.statement: IFC holds >30% share of net cash flows in Amarah project initially, then 30%
items.quote: Their percentage share in the cash flows of the project would be a little bit more than 30% in the net cash flows of the project till a certain figure they have a higher share and then becomes 30 %.

items.statement: Targets 27-30% gross profit margin on JV projects at current prices
items.quote: So based on current sale prices and current cost of construction, we typically look for about 27% to 30% on JV projects.

items.statement: Conservative pre-sales guidance due to potential launch delays and project underperformance
items.quote: We might have a launch delay. We don't know what all things go wrong. In my experience in life, there has been only one law that is always applied and that's been Murphy's law. So , we are conservative in that front.

items.statement: Term sheets have ~50% failure rate during diligence
items.quote: But these things are 50% as sometimes term sheets slip somewhere or the other during diligence or something or the other.

items.statement: FY25 profit growth target of at least 20% over FY24's Rs 1,388 crore
items.quote: I think going forward next year, we at least see if all goes well and there are not too many surprises, we should do greater than 20% growth for the year.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth target of 15-20% and earnings growth of ~20%
items.quote: I think we believe that we shall be able to grow top line wise also more than 15% to 20% and even on earnings growth, also, we are looking at about 20% comfortably.

items.statement: Agrochemicals internal target to triple revenue to Rs 300 crore in 3 years
items.quote: our internal target is that this business has to triple in the next 3 years, we want to go to Rs. 300 crores.

items.statement: Annual capex of Rs 300-350 crore for maintenance and incremental capacity at existing sites
items.quote: we expect that we should spend about Rs. 300 crores to Rs. 350 crores a year is what we are spending in a year.

items.statement: Expanding capacity at existing sites; no new greenfield sites planned
items.quote: We are not building any new sites. But in the existing site itself, we are expanding capacity.

items.statement: RoW business performing well with Brazil at $25-26M, Canada at ~CAD 40M, and strong orders from Egypt and Saudi
items.quote: Brazil, I think direct exports and our subsidiary exports are almost $25 million to $26 million a year. Canadian sub has done nearly CAD 40 million. So, overall, our RoW business is doing well. I think this year , we have some very good orders from Egypt and Saudi.

items.statement: Margins sustainable if product mix holds; conservative 20% PAT growth guidance despite stable margins and 15-20% revenue growth
items.quote: Based on the product mix holding up, yes.

items.statement: Revlimid pricing trajectory driven by market dynamics; no specific guidance on future pricing
items.quote: It goes by the market dynamics. I think that's the answer I can give you.

items.statement: Key pipeline products: Semaglutide (FTF on certain strengths), Olaparib, Carfilzomib, Trabectedin, Imbruvica (subject to litigation), Kyprolis
items.quote: Semaglutide we mentioned, Olaparib we have mentioned. Carfilzomib, we have mentioned; Trabectedin, we have mentioned. So, I think this is all there in the investor presentation.

items.statement: Filed Rimegepant for migraine but faces 7-8 day-one filers; targeting 2-3 first-to-file approvals in next 2 years
items.quote: we filed a product called Rimegepant for migraine. But it was like, I think, 7 or 8 filers on day 1.

items.statement: Revlimid U.S. distribution agreement with Teva continues beyond Jan 2026 settlement on same terms
items.quote: Yes, we have an arrangement with Teva that will continue.

items.statement: Cannot draw parallels between Canada and U.S. Revlimid markets due to different dynamics, partners, and REMS requirements
items.quote: Canada is a completely different market. I mean, how the product is distributed and how the tender cycles work. So, to answer your question, no, you can't draw parallels, it's a different world.

items.statement: Kothur plant under regulatory scanner; derisking via two U.S.-approved sites (Hyderabad, Vizag) and CMO model for niche products
items.quote: we have 2 sites for the U.S. So, we have Hyd erabad, and we have Vizag. So, like Rimegepant that we filed recently, we filed from Vizag

items.statement: Actively seeking RoW/emerging market acquisition to strengthen base business; valuations more attractive than India
items.quote: we are looking at an acquisition and, in the RoW,. I think that's what we are looking at.

items.statement: Buyback under consideration if large acquisition not concluded; decision pending
items.quote: if we get a large enough acquisition then I don't want to do a buyback. But if we are unable to close a large acquisition, then maybe we can consider a buyback.

items.statement: Net cash position: Rs 2,004 crore cash/investments vs Rs 116 crore debt (Rs 40 cr EPC credit, Rs 76 cr self-liquidating bill discounting)
items.quote: Rs. 2,004 crores is cash and listed shares and investments and deposits and Rs. 116 crores is the debt we have as of today, yes.

items.statement: Domestic business model change caused one-time Rs 35 cr charge; run rate remains ~Rs 100 cr/quarter, growing 8-10%
items.quote: It's a onetime charge because we just changed a few things and the way we are distributing. I think the run rate is still 95% to 100%.

items.statement: Agrochemicals one-time Rs 30 cr hit for non-utilized intermediate capacity at third-party site due to price drop
items.quote: we had to make a provision for non -utilization of that. So, we took a hit on depreciation of amo unt and certain advance we gave to that supplier.

items.statement: ~5,000 employees excluding contractors; ~5,700-5,800 including contractors; employee cost ratio expected to sustain
items.quote: if we remove the contractors,is what about 5,000 employees in the system and if we include the contractors and everyone, I think it's about 5,700 to 5,800.

items.statement: Conservative guidance due to unforeseen risks; one-offs can occur from inventory, currency, or other moving parts
items.quote: There's always something that you never know will happen, right? So, why promise something. The other person asked me, is there going to be another one time. There's always something that will go wrong, right?

items.statement: gCopaxone (glatiramer) steady with two generics (Sandoz and Natco); slight volume decline due to shift to oral MS therapies
items.quote: It's been consistent. I think it's done well. there are only 2 generics, Sandoz and us. So, Mylan has done extremely well with this product.

items.statement: NCE in Phase II for oral cancer; early stage, no guidance provided
items.quote: So, we have 1 NCE, which is doing Phase II in the U.S. at this time and it's in the early days, so I think I will refrain from giving any guidances or any idea.

items.statement: Cellogen CAR-T investment is modest, early-stage; option to invest more based on progress
items.quote: It's a very early stage. I can't get into timelines and all, but I think we are excited, and I think we see that there are a lot of opportunities in this area.

items.statement: Red Sea/logistics impact minimal as niche products shipped by air; freight cost not significant portion of product value
items.quote: Our whole model is only doing niche and a lot of our shipments are by air , and compared to the value, the air freight component is not a significant portion of the costing.

items.statement: Domestic pharma business growing 8-10%; secondary sales consistent near Rs 100 cr/quarter
items.quote: We believe the business is growing around 8% to 10%.

items.statement: Agrochemicals FY24 revenue fell Rs 25-30 cr short of Rs 140-150 cr target due to bad monsoon and returns
items.quote: We wanted to do about Rs. 140 crores to Rs. 150 crores. I think those are our estimations, we fell short and by about Rs. 25 crores, Rs. 30 crores.

items.statement: Base business PAT (ex-Revlimid) estimated at Rs 350-400 crore
items.quote: It is probably around maybe Rs. 350 crores to Rs. 400 crores PAT, I would believe, yes.

items.statement: Capex plan of INR200-300 crore in FY26 and INR300-400 crore in FY27, totaling INR600-700 crore over next 3 years
items.quote: Swati so looking at the current fleet size we would definitely like to have a capex plan of about INR200 crores to INR300 crores next year w hich is 25 -26 and then 26 -27 around INR300 crores, INR400 crores. So put together about INR600 crores, INR700 crores capex will go in next 3 years

items.statement: Major part of capex to be funded through internal accruals
items.quote: And we believe that we are doing good profitability currently and we should only grow our profitability. So major part of this capex will be funded through the internal accruals.

items.statement: Market rates firm for next 2-3 years; East Coast opportunities growing over 5-7 years with new ONGC discoveries; targeting one 3-year contract opportunity
items.quote: to add over the next 4 to 5 years? Naveen Mohta: Yes on the East Coast a lso there's a lot of requirement is coming up with new discoveries and new oil production being flowing from ONGC from East Coast. So there's one exciting opportunity which we are targeting as of now and which we are looking to if that opportunity happens then we will be getting a 3 year kind of contract for that

items.statement: Maintaining healthy working capital cycle of 80-90 days; current debtors equivalent to Q3 billing
items.quote: So we are maintaining a healthy working capital cycle of around 90 days which we are maintaining throughout t he period. If you see the current debt this is equivalent to Q3 billing both are more or less equal. So we are maintaining the healthy cycle of 80 to 90 days

items.statement: Charter rates improved vs last year; trend expected to continue for 2-3 years; benefit depends on vessel availability for spot market
items.quote: So over -- compared to last year we have seen prices forming up which are giving us an advantage and I foresee t his trend to continue for next two-three years definitely. But again it all depends upon how many vessels are available to take that advantage for the spot market

items.statement: 3 vessels on long-term charter, 3 on 2-year spot contracts; non-monsoon vessels idle in Q2 and part of Q1
items.quote: Out of 6 vessels, 3 are already on a long -term charter. The balance 3 are also on a spot contract for 2 -year basis. So, there is no deviation or volatility in terms of the profitability. Only the 3 contracts that I mentioned on the later part are on non -monsoon season.

items.statement: Opening global office in London via UK subsidiary; acquired property for this purpose with INR180 crore loan
items.quote: This loan we have given to our UK subsidiary and we are in the process of opening our global office there in London. For that we have acquired some property. For its funding we have provided that term loan.

items.statement: Seasonality impacts Q1 (monsoon from mid-May) and Q2; 3 non-monsoon vessels idle during this period; year-on-year growth expected despite seasonality
items.quote: Even in Q1, since the monsoon hits around 15th of May onwards, so our three vessels which are on non -monsoon season only operate, they will not be operating after two months of Q1 and entire Q2. But however, we believe that on a year -on-year basis, we should be doing better.

items.statement: Future capex (replacement vs new addition) depends on DG shipping guidelines 2 years out
items.quote: So that depends Swati depending on 2 years down the line how DG shipping guidelines will come and how vessels are available. So i t can be either a replacement or new addition depending on the market opportunity

items.statement: Targets 25-30% loan book growth for FY25
items.quote: So about 25% to 30% is what we are approximately targeting.

items.statement: Expects average credit cost of 2.5-3% on steady state basis
items.quote: on an ongoing basis, on a steady state on average we expect about 2.5% to 3% of credit costs going forward.

items.statement: Targets 60-75 new branches plus split branches in FY25
items.quote: we are targeting anywhere from about 60 to 75 new branches plus certain split branches as well

items.statement: Expects borrowing cost to decline by at least 100 bps
items.quote: At least we are expecting 100 bps dip as is the market interest rates.

items.statement: NIMs expected to be largely protected despite lending rate cuts
items.quote: NIMs would be largely protected.

items.statement: Targets comfortable capital adequacy of 22-25% (4.5x debt-to-equity)
items.quote: Typically, we target about 4.5x of debt to equity. That comes out to 22%-25%or so.

items.statement: Consolidated AUM grew 36% YoY to INR 2,639 crores as of March 2024
items.quote: As on 31st March 2024, Arman' s consolidated assets under management stood at INR2,639 crores, registering a growth of 36% has compared to INR1,943 crores on 31st March 2023.

items.statement: Microfinance AUM grew 35% YoY to INR 2,193 crores; MSME AUM grew 44% YoY
items.quote: Our Microfinance and MSME AUM reported 35% and 44% year-on-year growth, respectively.

items.statement: Standalone AUM grew 42% YoY to INR 446 crores including Two-Wheeler and Micro LAP pilot
items.quote: Our stand-alone assets under management, which includes lending to micro enterprise Two-Wheeler loans, and of course, the new Micro LAP pilot vertical increased by 42% to INR446 crores as compared to INR315 crores on 31st March 2023.

items.statement: Disbursements grew 30% YoY to approximately INR 2,300 crores in FY24
items.quote: Despite the rigorous screening process, we reported a 30% growth in disbu rsements amounting to approximately INR 2300 crores, driven by robust and consistent demand during the review period that is FY '24.

items.statement: Rural Micro LAP pilot expects INR 6-7 crores disbursement in Q1 FY25
items.quote: This quarter we are predicting about a INR6 crores or INR7 crores disbursement.

items.statement: FY24 consolidated NIM at 15.2%; yield at 25.1%; cost-to-income at 26.6%
items.quote: Yield stood at 25.1%. Net interest margin stood at 15.2%. Cost to income stood at 26.6%.

items.statement: All-inclusive borrowing cost ~13% for FY24; down 50-75 bps in Q4 post QIP and rating upgrade
items.quote: So Amit, all costed out, it turns out to be about 13 %-odd for the year. But post the QIP, we've already seen the rates coming down by about 50 bps to 75 bps in the last quarter

items.statement: Lending rates being cut due to competition and regulatory pressure; yields declining
items.quote: We are cutting our lending rates, of course, for competition and of course, through different pressure that is announced by regulato rs and other things. So definitely the REITs have gone down

items.statement: GNPA 2.88%, NNPA 31 bps as of March 2024; consolidated collection efficiency 96.6% in March
items.quote: Our gross non performing assets, which is GNPA, stood at 2.88% and net non performing assets, which is NNPA, were at a low of 31 basis points for period ended 31st March 2024. Collection efficiency for the month of March in our Microfinance business stood at 96.5%. MSME business stood at 97.6%, and our Two -Wheeler business stood at 95.6%. Consolidated collection efficiency stood at 96.6%.

items.statement: Collection pressure due to heat, elections, and over-lending in certain areas; expects recovery in next couple of quarters
items.quote: Overall there is some pressure on the collections. Numerous factors at play. Of course, there is heat and there is elections, but largely speaking there's a lot of -- I mean in certain areas there has been a lot of over lending going on and that has been generating pressure for us on the repayment side. So hopefully it's nothing permanent and we can get it fixed in the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: Write-offs ~INR 40-45 crores (MFI ~40 cr, standalone ~5 cr); incremental provisions ~INR 20-25 crores in FY24
items.quote: So that impairment cost of INR65 crores, if you had to attribute it to increase in provisions versus write-offs, what Vivek is saying around INR40 crores to INR45 crores would be write-offs and INR20 crores to INR25 crores would be provision -- increase in provisions.

items.statement: Cumulative provisions at INR 90 crores (3.4% of AUM); management overlay included
items.quote: Cumulative provisions stood at INR90 crores, which is 3.4% of the consolidated assets under management. of these provisions for the Arman stand-alone business stood at INR17 crores, and for the subsidiary Namra stood at INR73 crores.

items.statement: Opened 67 new branches in FY24; total branch count 402; expanded into newer states
items.quote: In terms of branch expansion, we have opened 67 new branches over the last 12 months, bringing our total branch count to 402 branches. This expansion has been complemented by successful penetration into newer states and geographies where performance has been promising.

items.statement: Total borrowings INR 2,261 crores; debt-to-equity 1.8x; cash/liquidity INR 180 crores; CAR standalone 62.7%, Namra 32.8%
items.quote: Total borrowings amounted to INR2,261 crores, comprising of a diverse mix of financial instruments. We maintained substantial liquidity of about INR180 crores in c ash and bank balance, liquid investments and undrawn CC limits with a comfortable debt-to-equity ratio of 1.8 times, and a healthy capital adequacy ratio of 62.7% on a stand-alone basis.

items.statement: ~75% of customers have loans from other institutions; over-leveraging risk due to FOIR assessment challenges
items.quote: I think only about 20% to 25% of the customers are new to credit or... Vivek Modi: Unique to us. Alok Patel: Or unique to us overall. 75% of our customers would have another loan from some other institutions, whether it is a Kisan credit loan or a tractor l oan or an MFI loan or gold loan or what have you, right

items.statement: MFI ticket size increased from INR 28k to INR 46-47k over 3 years; moved from 12 to 24-month tenure to keep EMI affordable
items.quote: Specifically for us, we started -- when I started M icrofinance in 2010, it was INR10,000, 1 -year loan. items.statement: Board approval for equity raise up to INR 250 crores, not yet executed
items.quote: I think we had already announced that we were looking for permission to raise equity up to INR 250 crores. We've not done anything yet on that but we have permission to raise equity up to INR 250 crores.

items.statement: Advertising spend at 7-8% of sales in FY24, similar planned for FY25
items.quote: It's going to be in the 7.5%. 7% to 8%.

items.statement: General trade largest channel, e-commerce second, weak in large format stores

items.statement: Team built for INR 2,000 cr scale; ESOPs and performance-linked compensation driving motivation
items.quote: We have, I would say, built a team for a INR 2,000 crores turnover while we are at INR 900 crores or even actually before that. So, our size of teams are bigger, probably, than our competitors. I think they're hungry. They're quite hungry for success because their compensation is linked to it. We also have, you know, ESOP schemes, which we give our people.

items.statement: New furnace ramp-up may pressure margins for 2-3 quarters; impact uncertain

items.statement: New pressware furnace peak sales potential INR 250-300 crores at full utilization

items.statement: Non-glassware: bottles and juicers leading growth; double-digit growth across most categories
items.quote: Bottles in general have done well. You know, your insulated bottles have done well. Things like, I think things like your juicers have done well, you know, I think there's a lot of focus on health, healthy products. And those products have done well for us.

items.statement: Non-glassware: #1-2 on Amazon in OTGs, juicers; strong in bottles via personalization; trade channels still developing

items.statement: Scientific division backward integration capex on hold; not under consumer entity
items.quote: At the moment, so that will now come under scientific division. That will not come here. So that's mainly for scientific. But that's on hold only. I don't think we are at the moment looking to get into that.

items.statement: No specific FY25 margin or revenue guidance given; focus on long-term over quarterly
items.quote: It's hard for me to give you specific numbers for FY '25. All I can say is that the Borosilicate furnace that we've added short-term may have some impact but I would say it would dramatically help improve EBITDA in, say, the coming year.

items.statement: Target ~10,000 homes delivered over FY25-27, with annual handovers rising from 3,500 in FY25
items.quote: We are very confident of sustaining a growth momentum both in terms of 3,500 units to be handed over in FY '25 as well as a target of roughly 10,000 homes to be delivered over the next three years, '25, '26 and '27.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin 23%, gross margin 34%, PBT margin ~7%, PAT Rs 75.4 cr; margins stabilized in mid-20s EBITDA, mid-30s gross, ~10% PBT
items.quote: EBITDA is at 23%, PBT is about 7%. Net profit is at about 75 crores, which is a new high for us. More importantly, as I said, margins have stabilized in the mid-20s at EBITDA level, mid-30s in the gross margin level and 10% in the PBT level.

items.statement: FY24 sales volume 4.59 msf (+14% YoY), sales value Rs 2,362 cr (+28% YoY), collections Rs 1,390 cr (+16% YoY), handovers 3,000+ homes (+50% YoY)

items.statement: Reaffirmed long-term revenue CAGR guidance of 25% over next 3-5 years, with gradual trajectory
items.quote: we stand with our revenue guidance of 25% CAGR over the next three to five years. But again, one should see that this is going to be more of a gradual trajectory towards moving towards the 25% CAGR growth.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA and PAT expected to grow faster than revenue driven by operational efficiencies and capacity utilization
items.quote: We also anticipate that our EBITDA and PAT will grow at a faster rate than revenue, driven by operational efficiencies and increased utilization across our units.

items.quote: Our EBITDA margins for FY '24 stood at 42.8% as compared to 40.5%, an increase of 230 bps. Our PAT margins for FY '24 stood at 30.3% as compared to 28.1%, an increase of 220 bps.

items.quote: Beyond a certain number, the delta would be there but it would be lower compared to what you would have seen when the capacity utilization was, say, at 10% or 15%.

items.statement: Major capex completed; only maintenance capex of ~INR 25 crores annually going forward
items.quote: Now we would have some bit of maintenance capex only which will be to the tune of INR25 crores or so. As, now as mentioned earlier also that this year as well as the coming year is more about how we optimally utilize the capacities that we have put in place.

items.statement: Limbasi facility utilization at 35.12% in FY24 vs 31.81% in FY23; injectable plant commercial production expected early H2 FY25
items.quote: Limbasi facility is working at around 35.12% in this financial year. It was 31.81% in the last financial year.

items.quote: we're expecting it to be somewhere in the early half of Q3.

items.statement: Immunosuppressant share reduced by ~4% YoY; oncology and anti-infectives growing faster
items.quote: compared to last year, the immunosuppressants have come down by around 4%, the weightage on immunosuppressants.

items.quote: We are pleased to announce the addition of two new products in the fermentation API space, bringing our total products count to 30. We also have a robust pipeline of over 10 products to be introduced in the coming years

Hence, we anticipate revenue normalization in FY'25.

items.statement: Formulation revenue grew 106% YoY in FY24 to INR 189 crores; domestic business grew 24%
items.quote: Our formulations revenue grew by 37% in Q4FY'24 and 106% for the full year FY'24 on a year-on-year basis.

items.quote: this was close to around -- probably around 6% to 7% or so.

items.statement: API revenue INR 828 crores (9% YoY), Formulation revenue INR 189 crores (106% YoY), Domestic revenue grew 24%, Export revenue grew 15%
items.quote: revenue from API business grew by 14% in this quarter and 9% for the full financial year 2024. It stood at INR 265 crores for this quarter and INR 828 crores for the financial year 2024

items.statement: FY24 revenue crossed INR 1,000 crores at INR 1,107 crores (19% YoY); EBITDA INR 435 crores (26% YoY); PAT INR 308 crores (28% YoY)
items.quote: Revenue from operations for the financial year 2024 crossed INR 1,000 crores and stood at INR1,107 crores against INR 853 crores in financial year 2023, representing growth of 19% as compared to the last year.

items.statement: Actively exploring CDMO opportunities with innovators and major generic players; submitting RFQs; not included in guidance

items.statement: Quarterly lumpiness in API sales due to customer procurement patterns; management recommends annual evaluation
items.quote: Revenue growth can be impacted on account of customers' procurement patterns, leading to lumpiness in sales in a particular quarter, causing fluctuations in sales.

items.statement: No significant raw material cost increases; some raw material costs reduced; no API pricing pressure seen
items.quote: we do not see any challenges either on the pricing front or any raw material or anything which has actually increased substantially in terms of the pricing. As a matter of fact we have been able to bring down, in certain cases, the cost of the raw materials which we were currently procuring.

items.statement: International revenue grew 15% YoY in FY24; new regulatory approvals opening emerging markets

items.statement: Expanded doctor reach by 1,000+ in FY24 across nephrology, oncology, rheumatology

items.statement: Aspires mid-teens revenue growth in FY25 backed by new store openings and subject to industry demand recovery; targets profitability improvement via cost efficiency
items.quote: To summarise, going ahead for FY '25 , the company aspires to achieve mid -teens revenue growth backed by new store openings in new and existing geographies and subject to recovery in the overall industry demand for premium and mid-premium brands.

items.statement: Intends to spend around 5% of revenues on branding and advertising going forward
items.quote: Going ahead, we will spend on around 5% of revenues on branding and advertising.

items.statement: Capex of INR35 crores each in FY23 and FY24 includes new store additions and renovation of old stores; warehouse capex of INR13-14 crores was incurred last year
items.quote: So, it is both the capex for new stores as well as renovation of the old stores. That keeps on happening every year. Some stores keep on getting renovating. Every year.

items.quote: During the year, we have added 52 EBO stores and we plan to add another 30 to 40 new stores in FY '25.

items.quote: The market for premium and mid -premium branded appar el continued to experience softened demand due to consumer behaviour influenced by an inflationary environment that curtailed discretionary expenditures while concurrently witnessing a surge in consumer spend towards travel and other essential purchases.

items.quote: We should be in that range.

items.statement: MBO channel revenue degrew ~2% for FY24; Q4 degrowth appearance due to higher voluntary return provision of 25% vs 14.4% prior year
items.quote: MBO channel for the year has degrown by around 2%.

items.quote: There has been an increase in advertisement expenses related to brand building and store openings and these upfront investments will strengthen the brand in the coming years. items.statement: Same-store sales growth (SSSG) of 3.9% YoY in Q4 FY24 and 0.6% YoY for full year FY24
items.quote: Our SSSG for the year stood at 0.6% year -on-year.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR0.50 per share on face value of INR2 each
items.quote: The Board of Directors have recommended a final dividend of INR0.50 per share on face value of INR2 each of the company.

items.statement: Voluntarily increased expected goods return provision to 25% in Q4 FY24 from 14.4% in Q4 FY23, creating ~INR21 crores excess provision impacting gross profit, EBITDA, PBT by ~INR11.8 crores and PAT by ~INR9 crores
items.quote: In Q4 FY '23 , this provision was at 14.4% of sales whereas in Q4 FY '24 it has been voluntarily taken at 25% instead of 14.4% considering the increased returns due to the current market scenario. This has led to an excess provision of approximately INR 21 crores which has an approximate INR 11.8 crores impact on gross profit, EBITDA and PBT and an impact of INR9 crores on PAT.

items.statement: Market conditions remain volatile; April was good but May demand dwindled; difficult to predict immediate recovery; moderated growth ambitions to protect profitability

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend INR0.50 per share (face value INR2) for FY24

Slightly higher some, slightly lower in some years. But generally, around the 15% mark, mostly on the higher side. So, we would expect to be i n the same zone in the years to come.

items.statement: Expects better performance from subsidiaries from Q2 onwards.
items.quote: I would expect much better performance from Q2 onwards.

items.statement: Aims to turn Abhinava Rizel into INR1000 crores turnover in next decade.
items.quote: Our target, not just internal as you stated, is to turn this into a couple of INR1000 crores of turnover in the next decade.

items.statement: Export markets remain bleak with excessive Chinese price competition; domestic demand better than supply side
items.quote: The past year has been a challenging period for the agrochemical industry and overall export scenario still appears bleak.

items.statement: Chinese manufacturers offering products near Indian cost of production, pressuring export margins
items.quote: Quite a few products are being oﬀered by Chinese industry at price points near the cost of production of Indian agrochemical industry, making it diﬃcult to maintain proﬁtability margins in such an environment

items.statement: Domestic agrochemical brand business reported decent growth in FY24 and expects improvement in FY25
items.quote: The silver lining continues to be our domestic agrochemical brand business, where Aimco has reported decent growth in FY24 and it is further expecting improvement in FY25.

items.statement: Launched dozen new products and expanded marketing in Kerala and Rajasthan for domestic brand business
items.quote: In line with our focus on this segment, company has launched dozen new products and expanded its marketing in Kerala and Rajasthan.

items.statement: Three new molecules achieved desired purity yields; material scale-up expected in FY26
items.quote: We have three new products for commercialization in pipeline where the desired purity yields have been achieved, the ramp up remains subject to market condition and progress on product registration eﬀorts among these other aspects

items.statement: Revenue from new molecules to start from Q2 FY25 brand sales; full commercialization impact in FY26
items.quote: From Q2 this year onwards, we will see revenue starting from our brand sale business , and once we ramp up production Q2 onwards, the full impact of these three new molecules will be in the coming ﬁnancial year

items.statement: Witnessed 15-20% price increase in Chlorpyrifos due to raw material shortage and higher Chinese import prices
items.quote: We have witnessed about 15% to 20% price increase in that molecule, mainly because one of the raw material s is in short supply and some of the Chinese import prices of these raw materials has increased and because of that the prices have shown uptrend

items.statement: Two Brazil product registrations in final evaluation; expect receipt in FY25 but volume impact only in FY26
items.quote: As far as Brazil is concerned, two of our registrations are in the ﬁnal process of evaluation. We expect both the registrations to be received in this ﬁnancial year. But the advantage of these registrations will be reﬂecting in increased business volume only in next

items.statement: Taken possession of two MIDC plots; one for formulation facility for domestic brands in FY25, other for technical manufacturing for future pipeline
items.quote: We have taken possession of both the plots which we were allocated and now we are in the process of signing the lease agreement with MIDC and everything. So it's almost complete.

items.statement: Targeting 25% increase in domestic brand sales to ~Rs 75 crore in FY25 with 30-35% gross margin
items.quote: In FY25, we are targeting 25% increase in our brand sale business and to complement that, we have already launched several new molecules in our brand and there are additional few molecules which are already under registration process which we are going to launch within the next few months.

items.statement: Triclopyr contract manufacturing volumes up ~40% YoY but selling price down 40-45%, limiting topline improvement
items.quote: So contract manufacturing volumes have increased almost by 40% over the previous year . But the issue is that the selling price of Triclopyr has substantially come down as compared to the previous year and that's why there was no signiﬁcant improvement in top line

items.statement: Triclopyr volumes forecast similar to FY24; pricing remains challenging due to Chinese competition
items.quote: The forecast we have received also is in the similar volumes as compared to last year and forecast which we have received from our other markets where we have direct customers also is very strong in volumes. But the pricing of the product is in a diﬃcult situation in competition with China

items.statement: Chlorpyrifos volumes ~1,800 tons in FY24; expect ~25% volume growth in FY25 with improving margins
items.quote: We did about 1,800 tons last year and we expect these volumes to substantially improve this year.

items.statement: Targeting minimum 25% overall topline growth in FY25; may revise higher as season progresses
items.quote: We are targeting 25% improvement over the last year sales, and as the season progresses, we will change our target to even higher number, but minimum 25% growth we are expecting this year.

items.statement: Herbicide plant (14-step process) not dropped; process development complete; patents expiring next year; ramp-up in FY26
items.quote: The process development is already over. The registration process is going on. There are patents related to the process on the molecule which are expiring next year so we are working on the product at the moment and actual ramp up production of those molecules will be in FY26.

items.statement: Currently manufacturing 3 technical molecules; will reach 6 after adding 3 new molecules
items.quote: So currently we are manufacturing three molecules and after adding these three new molecules we will be manufacturing six molecules.

items.statement: At least one new contract manufacturing molecule to commercialize in FY25; volumes unclear yet
items.quote: At least one of them I'm positive we will be able to commercialize this year.

items.statement: Discussing new contract manufacturing customers beyond UPL; no definite agreements yet
items.quote: We are discussing at the moment, but I don't have a deﬁnite answer so that we can say anything with certainty, we are discussing

items.statement: FY24 revenue INR2,177 crore, EBITDA margin 21.1%, exceeded INR2,000 crore and 20% margin targets
items.quote: We exceeded our projected target of INR2,000 crores in revenue and a 20% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Target INR3,000 crore revenue by FY26 with 20%+ EBITDA margin
items.quote: It is still achievable. I mean, last year, we had projected INR2,000 crores and we landed up at INR2,177 crores. So, we did across our projection. I believe in the next 2 years, we'll definitely touch INR3,000 crores.

items.statement: Expect 15% volume growth in FY25
items.quote: Yes, yes. Definitely. 15% is achievable.

items.statement: Expect to double US revenue from $100M to $200M in 1-2 years
items.quote: Well, in a short-term point of view, from a short -- from a span of maybe 1 to 2 years, we are looking at doubling our revenue. So, if we are getting $100 million, a little at $200 million.

items.statement: Sustainable gross margin range 50-52%
items.quote: So, we expect the gross margins to remain in the range of between say 50% to 52% on a sustainable basis.

items.statement: R&D spend around 2% of sales in FY25
items.quote: No 2%. I would say 2% is more reasonable.

items.statement: Capex FY25 ~INR100-125 crore including INR75 crore for Teva phase 2
items.quote: So we will be putting in another INR75-odd crores into Teva and then the nominal capex, which goes on to all our plants that whether it's U.S. or earlier plants, we normally do nominal capex, which goes to about INR25 crores on per plant.

items.statement: FY24 capex INR208 crore: INR125 crore Teva, INR30 crore Goa, INR31 crore US, INR22 crore UK
items.quote: The capex incurred during the period was INR208 crores, which increased INR125 crores in the acquired facility from Teva Pharma, INR30 crores in the existing Goa facility, INR31 crores in the U.S. facility, and INR22 crores in the U.K. manufacturing facilities.

items.statement: Teva plant phase 1: 3 billion tablets installed, commercialized; phase 2: 5+ billion tablets by H2 FY25
items.quote: The first phase was 3 billion tablets and which we have achieved installing this capacity. So now we are scaling up to utilize this capacity and we will probably have that additional revenue, which comes out of 3 billion. But in the FY '25, we plan to increase this capacity towards the second half of FY '25 to 5 billion.

items.statement: Teva plant capacity utilization very low currently, improving from April 2024
items.quote: See, the capacity -- we are in the process of increasing the capacity of the new facility. So in terms of the capacity utilization right now, it is very low. But from this month -- see April onwards, we have started utilizing the newer capacities as well.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 19.6% down 17.6% QoQ due to freight surge and Teva costs
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the quarter was 19.6%. The sequential decline is due to the surge in freight cost, due to the Red Sea crisis from January '24 and the increase in expenses related to the Teva acquisition.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin 21.1%, up 274 bps YoY
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 21.1%, a 274 basis point improvement over the previous year.

items.statement: US EBITDA margin ~10%+, expected to improve with operating leverage
items.quote: See, we are at -- like we are at 10% plus EBITDA margin in the U.S. as well in terms of our overall U.S. portfolio. And that stands -- that is going to increase.

items.statement: Teva plant expected to break even at EBITDA level in Q1 FY25
items.quote: I think from this quarter itself we should be breaking even. Agastya Dave: At an EBITDA level

items.statement: US order book healthy, provides visibility for revenue doubling
items.quote: Our order book status is quite healthy. So we have a good order book status to give us visibility of reaching to this number.

items.statement: Freight rates doubled in Q4 due to Red Sea crisis, cost impact ~INR9 crore
items.quote: The transit time and freight rates almost doubled in Q4 as compared to Q3 due to the Red Sea crisis. This escalation impacted the cost of approximately INR9 crores.

items.statement: Increased US warehouse inventory by ~INR7 crore to mitigate supply chain risk
items.quote: This decision has resulted in an increase in our stock reserves by approximately INR7 crores while consolidation of the account.

items.statement: Debt-free with INR674 crore cash as of March 31, 2024
items.quote: We continue to remain debt-free and have a total of INR674 crores of cash as of 31st March 2024.

items.statement: Ibuprofen ~15% of revenue; global market share >15%
items.quote: I would say we are approximately about 15% of contribution comes from this molecule, one point. Nirali Shah: Okay. And the market share? Mark Saldanha: Again, depending on which market we are talking about but it will pretty much be at above 15% maybe of the market share

items.statement: US revenue mix: OTC 80%, Rx 20%
items.quote: See, broadly, the mix in our U.S. revenue for OTC 80% and Rx is around 20%.

items.statement: US growth driven by existing and new customers; wallet share increase with existing customers
items.quote: It's a mix of both. Our order book status is quite healthy. So we have a good order book status to give us visibility of reaching to this number. And -- but it is a growth on existing plants as well as new customers coming in.

items.statement: Goa facility USFDA observations: normal, replied, no operational impact expected
items.quote: I don't see any impact on our operations, number one. Number two is, obviously, we replied to all the observations. And we don't foresee any issues in the observations.

items.statement: Europe entry via M&A: advanced dialogue but nothing concrete
items.quote: We are in dialogue. We are in advanced dialogue but nothing concrete right now. But we are hoping the optimistic we're hoping. M&A is such an unpredictable thing even when we come to the last step it may not happen.

items.quote: It would be close to 400 acres capacity expansion across multiple units across various product lines. items.quote: Close to 83% to 85% at that level.
