items.quote: Mostly, it is raw material. We tend to be light as a strategy on finished goods. Unless it's a strategic decision where a shipment is being planned or we see there's going to be a price resurgence. But you could assume that more than 60% is raw material.

items.statement: Long-term debt reduced to INR83 crores, debt-to-equity 0.16; comfortable leveraging up to 0.6x for future capex
items.quote: On financial front, our long-term debt has reduced to about INR83 crores with a very low debt to equity ratio of 0.16.

items.quote: We are prioritizing high er starch utilization. We strive for optimal performance, maximizing operational efficiency and boosting productivity across our operations

items.quote: As far as pricing is concerned, we negotiate as a -- it's our company policy not to get into any fixed-term, long-term contracts which are forward-looking. We negotiate on the day when we are ready to place an order of a certain quantity or for a certain period.

items.statement: Export opportunity driven by China+1, PLI scheme, and India's cost competitiveness; servicing paper/textile demand shifting to India/Southeast Asia
items.quote: See, this whole reliance of Making in India, more product in India, PLI scheme was a big push for Indian products being -- food products being exported as global challenges -- as global challenges of supply chain and the China plus 1 for ingredients and India being favorably placed in terms of both self-growth within India and export-led growth to our neighboring countries.

items.statement: Maize price volatility and FMCG/pharma demand recovery pace are key uncertainties for margins and top-line growth
items.quote: However, what I cannot predict is how maize pricing will be forward looking beyond one season.

items.statement: Order book grew 85% YoY to Rs 964 Crores, 3.6x FY24 revenue
items.quote: We started financial year '24 with an order book of almost Rs 521 Crores and as it peaks, the new orders of 760 Crores in the year till end of March 2024. Our current outstanding order book stands at approximately Rs 964 Crores, a strong growth of 85% year-on-year and translates into 3.6x of our Financial Year 2024 revenue.

items.statement: Defense segment forms 86% of order book at Rs 834 Crores
items.quote: The company's current order book stands at Rs 965 Crores, out of which the defense segment forms the majority Rs 834 Crores, which is 86% of the total order book.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance 18-21% for FY25
items.quote: The margins will be in the same line because the same business will continue in the same way. Will be in the range of 18% - 20% - 21% of EBITDA for the year ending '25.

items.statement: No formal revenue guidance but expects improvement from current order book
items.quote: Normally, we do not give any guidance. But based on the existing order book and the time line, we should be able to come -- I mean, some -- maybe some good improvement from now.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 operating margin 17.4%, up 189 bps YoY

items.statement: FY24 operating margin 21.5%, up 875 bps YoY

items.quote: Right now, our target is going into expanding our raw material capacity, manufacturing capacity to meet the present international demand and also the new areas that we are expanding in the aerospace as well as ammunition space. These are the areas where we are going to grow, Capex is going in that area.

items.statement: 60% of QIP proceeds for capex, rest for debt repayment
items.quote: A significant amount out of this we have proposed will be used for Capex and some portion will be used for the repayment of existing debt.

items.quote: The Orissa government has issued a letter to Orissa Industrial Development Corporation to identify land for allotment to Premier. But now, next week onwards again from June month onwards the activit

items.statement: Existing capacity sufficient for current order book; capex for future orders
items.quote: Present order book, execution, our existing capacities are sufficient. The capacity is not for these orders. These are -- the Capex is for the future order. This is not going to affect the present production supplies.

items.statement: Defense revenue share rose from 40% to 62% in FY24, targeting 75-80%
items.quote: Basically, if you see our presentation, the current year, I think our total defense contribution came at 62%. So -- which has gone up from 40% to 62% when compared to last year which will be -- I think we shall reach about 75% to 80% going forward.

items.statement: Detonator production 10 million in FY24, expected zero next year due to PESO limits
items.quote: Detonators is a market which is going out. So the quantities are not decided by us. They are decided by PESO and they are giving a limit, and we are selling up to the limit we have given. So next financial year, it is going to be 0.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of Rs 2.50 per share for FY24
items.quote: In line with our policy to reward our shareholders, Board of Directors have recommended a dividend Rs 2.50 per share. However, the same will be subject to the approval of shareholders.

items.statement: Countermeasure orders execution started, significant billing in H1 FY25

items.quote: Yes, we are participating, I think, in about Rs 700 crore, Rs 800 Crores if I remember offhand. We are expecting that at least Rs 500 Crores are part of it, that at least 60% - 70% will materialize, that's what we are thinking.

items.statement: Only Indian company qualified for countermeasures and exporting fully assembled rocket motors
items.quote: Future outlook of Premier Explosive is Premier is the only qualified Indian company for counter measures, and the only Indian company which specializes in the export of fully assembled rocket motor.

And after that, a lot of validation takes place for the product before the end

items.quote: There is a change in the time line also. We have also requested for extension of the date because of the present international maritime problems. Some of the ingredients, which are imported and they are delayed, so it is being considered.

items.statement: Expects revenue to reach INR 2,000 crores per annum in the near future, within 18 months.
items.quote: So, I expect to achieve at least a revenue of INR 2,000 crores per annum in the future, in the near future. This is my planning.

items.statement: Expects quarterly revenue to increase from INR 400 crores to INR 600-650 crores within 18 months.
items.quote: So, I expect within the next 18 months, we can do from INR 400 crores revenue to about INR 600 crores, INR 650 crores revenue in a quarter.

items.statement: Margins are expected to continue in the 10% to 15% range.
items.quote: See our style is what you ca n see in the past, we are normally working between a margin of 10% to 15%. So that should be continued

items.statement: Freight costs have stabilized and largely passed on to customers.

items.statement: Expects trade route disruptions to normalize, leading to revenue and profitability rebound.

items.statement: Value-added business including diabetic and brown rice doubled revenues.

items.statement: Avoids high-risk territories like Iran and limits exposures in Iraq.
items.quote: At Chaman Lal Setia, our strategic focus on profitable growth and secure cash flows, whereas to avoid high-risk territories like Iran and limit exposures in Iraq.

items.statement: Net debt fully repaid as of today; cash flows expected positive in Q1 and Q2.

items.statement: Inventory of INR 499 crores is largely order booked.

items.statement: Expects DCD to achieve double-digit growth in FY25

items.statement: Plans to open offices in Delhi, Mumbai and Bangalore for EVA corporate sourcing
items.quote: We are planning to open an office in Delhi, Bangalore and maybe later going to say Bombay. For sourcing more corporates for the EVA product.

items.statement: Mauritius Fund invested INR10 crores via warrants; INR2.5 crores received, balance INR7.5 crores by H1 FY25
items.quote: Mauritius Fund has invested about INR10 crores in our share of the warrants issue, INR2.5 crores they already put in. And I think then, say, before the end of the next, this thing, half year closing, they put the balance of INR7.5 crores.

items.statement: Main challenge is corporate onboarding taking ~1.5 months and low product awareness
items.quote: That is a major challenge. That is what onboarding an employer takes about one and a half months with currently with us.

items.statement: EVA charges 2-2.5% upfront processing fee; business loans at 17-18%
items.quote: We charge about 2%, or 2.5% processing fees is deducted upfront.

items.statement: SBI sanctioned INR15 crore limit at 10.95%; debt-to-equity target 2:1
items.quote: Last year we were sanctioned limit by State Bank of India. And they have sanctioned a INR15 crore limit. Out of that, we have just placed only INR6 crores.

items.statement: Announcing one or two new business lines in 7-10 days
items.quote: I think we should be able to tell the exchange in the next 7-10 days.

items.statement: Management maintains ~20% revenue growth guidance for FY25 including some contribution from particle board plant
items.quote: So on the guidance, I think we still are maintaining about a 20% revenue growth with some value of revenue coming in from the particle board plant.

items.statement: Laminate volume growth expected in double digits over next few years
items.quote: And on the outlook, we think we should grow in double digits in volume over the next few years.

items.statement: Particle board plant capex of INR250-275 crore in FY25 plus INR50 crore maintenance capex; routine maintenance capex ~INR50 crore annually thereafter
items.quote: So this year, since the particle board unit is under implementation, so we expect around INR250 crores, INR275 crores in this year and another around INR50 crores of maintenance capex in this year. Going forward, the -- after the particle board unit put into place, so then you can expect around INR50 crores of capex -- maintenance capex on a routine basis.

items.statement: Peak net debt expected at INR925-950 crore in FY25
items.quote: We expect it to be in the range of around INR925 crores to INR950 crores in this year. That will be the peak debt -- peak net debt, which we are hoping.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 12.8% in FY24; expected to stay in this range or improve as new categories stabilize
items.quote: The blended margin this year is at 12.8%, and we believe that this should be in this range, or it will go up as and when the new product category, which we are into, may stabilize and start contributing more in terms of the margin.

items.statement: Particle board segment targeting 20-24% EBITDA margin by year 4 of operations
items.quote: We are expecting this to happen, the 20%, 25% -- 20%, 24% within fourth year of operation.

items.statement: Domestic demand slow across building material categories; export market share gains continuing despite Red Sea disruptions
items.quote: being a bit slow in terms of demand and all that stuff, as we've been hearing from our partners and teams and I'm sure you all have also heard that commentary from other building material industries. On the export front, too, I think we are winning more market share. The data we have. The exports from India has largely been flattish, and we won market share

items.statement: No price hikes planned for laminates and veneers; price hikes planned for plywood business
items.quote: So no price hikes have been planned for Lam and Allied and Veneer Allied. Price hikes have been planned for plywood business.

items.statement: Laminate Q4 FY24 production 5.21 million sheets, sales 5.23 million sheets; FY24 production 19.85 million, sales 18.97 million sheets
items.quote: Production volumes were the highest at 5.21 million sheets and at a utilization level of 85% on the enhanced capacity of 24.52 million. Sales volume for the quarter also was highest and stood at 5.23 million sheets.

items.statement: Working capital cycle improved to 60 days in Q4 FY24 from 72 days in Q3 FY24; net debt INR834 crore as of March 31
items.quote: In the current quarter, working capital cycle improved by 12 days to 60 days as compared to 72 days in the quarter 3 of this year. Net debt as on March 31 stood at INR834 crores as against INR847 crores in -- on December 31.

items.statement: Uttar Pradesh land acquired; approvals process underway; no concrete expansion plan yet
items.quote: So we're in the process of getting all the approvals in place, et cetera, but that's the stage we're at on the Uttar Pradesh plant.

items.statement: Board declared final dividend of INR1.65 per share (face value INR1) for FY24
items.quote: Board has declared a final dividend of INR1.65 per share of a face value of INR1.

items.statement: Revenue growth to be volume-led, better than market growth rate.
items.quote: So, look, our revenue growth in last few years is primarily driven by two-third by volume growth and will continue the same trend going forward, it will be largely driven by volume.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improvement expected to continue due to service mix, payer mix, and operating leverage.
items.quote: EBITDA margin that we see in Q4 is on account of better service mix and a payer mix and operating leverage due to a strong revenue growth. We expect that to continue going forward.

items.statement: Maintenance capex guided at Rs 65-70 crores.
items.quote: As far as the maintenance CAPEX is concerned, we have always guided, and our maintenance CAPEX will be around 65 to 70 crores and 70 crores is the number which you saw for FY'24 as well.

items.statement: North Bangalore center total capex estimated at Rs 90 crores, spent over current and next financial year.
items.quote: North Bangalore, the total CAPEX is estimated is around 90 crores which largely would be spent in the current year and of course in the next financial year.

items.statement: Effective tax rate for FY25 expected between 35% to 39%.
items.quote: Somewhere between 35% to 39%.

items.statement: Adding 350 to 400 beds in existing hospitals over next four to five years, mostly completed in three years.
items.quote: In total, across our current hospitals, we are looking at adding about 350 to 400 beds in our existing hospitals in the next four to five years. Most of that will get completed in the next three years.

items.statement: Two new hospitals in Bangalore with total 125 beds to be operational in next 12 to 15 months.
items.quote: We are currently in the process of establishing two hospitals with total 125 beds in North Bangalore and Whitefield area , slated to be operational in the next 12 to 15 months.

items.statement: South Mumbai expected to break even in middle of the year.
items.quote: South Mumbai has reduced the losses and is expected to start breaking even sometime in the middle of the year.

items.statement: Kolkata center started contributing positive EBITDA and will continue to grow.
items.quote: Kolkata has started contributing positive EBITDA. It will continue to grow going forward.

items.statement: Rising incidence of cancer expected in coming decade due to population and lifestyle.
items.quote: Given the population of India and more recognition of cancer and lifestyle disease, there is definitely going to be a rising incidence of cancer in the coming decade.

items.statement: Digital revenue grew 75% year-on-year in FY24 and will be important growth driver.
items.quote: Our digital revenue has grown 75% year-on-year in FY'24 and will continue to be an important driver of growth in future.

items.statement: Doctor attrition low at less than 5%, not expected to be an issue.
items.quote: our top doctors’ attrition is very low, less than 5%. So, we have been very proud and even today because of the way we empower the doctors, we are involved in academics and research. Our attrition has not been a major issue and we don't expect it to be an issue at all.

items.statement: Planning to introduce MR LINAC Radiation Therapy in Bangalore.
items.quote: We plan to introduce MR LINAC Radiation Therapy in Bangalore, which would be a notable addition to the vastly superior radiation treatment offering at a HCGwhich will help us revolutionize radiation therapy in the state.

items.statement: Institutional Research Committee established to fund investigator-initiated trials.
items.quote: We have established an Institutional Research Committee to fund investigator-initiated trials, which is one-of-a-kind in the Indian private health sector.

items.statement: Mortality rate now under 1%.
items.quote: We're happy to report that our mortality rate as we measure while we are one of the few measuring it has now come under 1% over the years , the feat we are immensely proud of and definitely meeting or beating the global standards.

items.statement: Management aims to consistently deliver growth and performance, with multi-year contracts for next year higher than current revenue.
items.quote: The contracts in the next year are much higher than, the current numbers that we have done.

items.statement: Management does not see margins declining due to favorable exchange rates, productivity, reusable components, and larger multi-year contracts.
items.quote: On a year-on-year basis, we do not believe that our margins will at all go down because everything is in favor the exchange rates are in favor, the productivity is in favor, reusable components and tools are in favor.

items.statement: Robust pipeline of signed businesses and multi-year contracts position the company for continued success.
items.quote: With a robust pipeline of signed businesses, we are well equipped to continue our trajectory of success in the upcoming year.

items.statement: Multi-year contracts signed for next year exceed current year revenue, providing revenue visibility.
items.quote: What we continuously and consistently try and achieve is that we have more signed contracts in hand for the next year before we end the current financial year.

items.statement: Capex is not a large portion of growth; investment focuses on talent, subsidiaries, market expansion, and potential acquisitions.
items.quote: Capex does not remain a very large portion of where the growth is done but investment does happen in creating subsidiaries, reaching out to new mark ets, reaching out to creating acquisitions or investments into scale-up startups

items.statement: Team grew from 250 to 400 engineers; targeting 40-60% year-on-year team growth, potentially doubling in 12 months.
items.quote: We do believe that on a year-on-year basis, we do add between 40%, to 60% of our team size. So, we are fairly geared at this point of time to grow from 400 to more than double in the next 12 months.

items.statement: Cybersecurity practice is a focus area with SOCs being set up in India and Netherlands for real-time monitoring.
items.quote: Shortly, we'll be setting up a Securities Oper ations Center, a SOC, in both India and the Netherlands. This is where a fa ir amount of investment will also

items.statement: 95% revenue from overseas (Nordics, Benelux, Germany, UK), 5% domestic; no single customer >20% of revenue.
items.quote: Almost 95% of our revenue comes from overseas customers and around 4%-5% comes from domestic customers.

items.statement: Shift to local entity in Netherlands enables higher billing rates and larger multi-year deals.
items.quote: This strategic shift from an outsourcing Company to a local entity in a local market, delivering local relationships and local culture, has significantly boosted our revenue and growth and enabled us to close larger multi-year deals.

items.statement: Active treasury desk hedges FX flows for at least 3 years.
items.quote: We at least make sure that we are fairly covered for at least 3 years. And we have a very active treasury desk towards making sure that we maintain our FX flows.

items.statement: Key risks include geopolitical instability, customer acquisition, technology changes; mitigated by diversification, FX hedging, and customer concentration limits.
items.quote: Somewhere war happens or somewhere political instability happens or the law changes in certain countries or your customers' businesses get acquired overnight and you lose control on your relationship.

items.statement: R&D spend estimated at 4-4.5% of revenue (INR4-5 crores in FY24), expensed not capitalized.
items.quote: Around INR4 crores to INR5 crores, yes.

items.statement: Priority is reinvestment for growth; dividend decision rests with board, but management recommends staying highly invested in growth.
items.quote: I would recommend to my board of directors to remain highly invested into growth and make sure that our shareholders remain as our top priority and we give them maximum growth along with the organization's growth.

items.statement: Competes with firms like Sogeti, TEOTO in Nordics/Benelux; differentiation via consulting depth, onsite presence, non-English market expertise.
items.quote: We compete with, let's say, Sogeti from France or we compete with TEOTO and every kind of players in the Nordics or we compete with a few names in the Benelux ecosystem.

items.statement: Stable Indian government supports global respect for Indian tech companies.
items.quote: Hopefully, if our results happen the way they are of our country, we get stable government. That means a lot to us on a global scale because Indian tech Company is hugely respected and appreciated on a global scale.

items.statement: Potential acquisitions or investments in scale-up startups are part of immediate strategies.
items.quote: investment does happen in creating subsidiaries, reaching out to new mark ets, reaching out to creating acquisitions or investments into scale-up startups and so on and so forth which do remain as some of the immediate strategies

items.statement: Q4 FY24 gross margin 46.2%, up 180 bps YoY; FY24 gross margin 45.4%, up 350 bps YoY
items.quote: Gross margin for the quarter stood at 46.2%, up by 180 basis points year-on-year as higher contribution from retail led to favourable product mix.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 11.7%, up 140 bps YoY; FY24 EBITDA margin 11.5%, up 50 bps YoY
items.quote: Operating EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 11.7%, up by 140 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: Expect margins to improve with softening raw material prices
items.quote: Looking ahead, we expect our margins to improve with the softening of key raw material prices.

items.statement: FY25 margin to remain more or less same as no price hikes planned; focus on volume growth
items.quote: Margin will be more or less same because we're not taking any price hikes. We want to increase the volume.

items.statement: Target retail revenue ₹650-700 cr in 3 years with EBITDA margin 17-18%
items.quote: We have an annual growth plan of around 12%-15% in the retail segment. And we are having an EBITDA margin of around 16% to 17%. So with the growth coming back in the retail, we expect to be around ₹650 crores to ₹700 crores in retail and EBITDA margin of around 17% to 18%.

items.statement: Plan to open 25 COCO and 70 franchisee stores in FY25, expecting 6-7% value growth from expansion
items.quote: We will be opening around 25 COCO and around 70 Franchisees. So, we expect in our value terms, around 6% to 7% growth from this expansion.

items.statement: 22 stores to be refurbished in FY25, phased quarterly with 8 in Q1, 8 in Q2, then 6 more after review
items.quote: will see in first quarter, we'll do around 8 refurbishings and see what is the impact of the refurbishing. Then again, we'll go for another 8. So we will -- during the -- out of 22, for the first 2 quarters, we'll do 16. And then we'll check how it's doing, then we'll go for the next 6

items.statement: Total store count 868 in FY24 (223 COCO, 645 franchisee); added 94 stores during the year
items.quote: During the year, we added 94 stores bringing our total count to 868 stores in FY '24. Breaking it down by model, our COO store count stands at 223 stores, while the franchisee model had 645 stores.

items.statement: Distribution network 753 distributors (+81 added in FY24); east zone has 482 distributors
items.quote: Our distribution network includes 753 distributors with an addition of 81 distributors this year. The east zone remains particularly strong with 482 distributors.

items.statement: Demand remains muted in Q4 and April-May due to heatwave, elections, macro conditions; expect pickup post-elections and festive season
items.quote: In regard to demand in retail, it is muted, still , t here are 2-3 reasons for that. One is the macroeconomic conditions, other is that we are basically in the eastern part of the country, where in the month of April, the continuous period of heat wave going on, which has really restricted the footfall in the stores. Second, there is a month long process of votes going on throughout the country, w

items.statement: No price hike taken in Q4 FY24 due to muted demand; kept running product prices intact
items.quote: We have not taken any price hike because, since the demand is muted, again, taking a price hike may also impact the volume. So, we have kept the price -- I mean, we have changed some products -- new product has come in AW -- when the festi ve thing with the new price range. But basically all the older products, which are running products, we have not taken a price hike seeing the lull in the deman

items.statement: May cut prices in lower segment (below ₹500) to regain volume lost to unorganized sector
items.quote: What we are thinking maybe in this -- I mean, the lower segment, we may a little bit cut down the prices and bring back the volume so that the overall sales of the company increases.

items.statement: Retail contribution 61% in Q4, 65% in FY24; distribution 35% in Q4, 31% in FY24
items.quote: Retail sales contributed 61% in Q4FY24 and 65% for the full fiscal year.

items.statement: Sub-brands share increased to 59% in FY24 from 57% in FY23; premium price points (>₹1,400) growing strongly
items.quote: The sub-brands last year was around 57% and this year, it is around 59%.

items.statement: BIS regulations implemented; pre-BIS inventory largely liquidated but some remains; extension given to micro/small units (≤₹5 cr revenue) for 1 year
items.quote: BIS inventory, there has been time given to liquidate the stock also. So, most of the stocks have been sold. Some stocks are there. That is also we are trying to sell it out and discounts are given in the EOSS season.

items.statement: Distribution sales reduced ~₹30 cr YoY as conscious call to reduce receivables; expect distribution sales to recover to FY23 levels in FY25
items.quote: Yes, in distribution I think last year -- from last year, we have -- the sale has reduced around ₹ 30 crores in Distribution. This is a genuine call taken by us to reduce our receivables also. But this year, I think the product category also changed. We ha ve introduced new products and in the Distribution that product is in demand. So , I think this year, we will be able to do a sale of what we h

items.statement: Plan to reduce inventory days and debtor days; working capital to remain at current level as COCO:franchisee ratio stays ~60:40
items.quote: We'll definitely try to reduce the inventory days and the debtors days. But it will be because the ratio remains the same. So, working capital also remains the same.

items.statement: Management aims for healthy growth in EBITDA and PAT in FY25 versus FY24, but declines to give specific top-line growth numbers.
items.quote: I would not like to speculate in specific numbers. It's early on, but I can say with confidence that we are a bottom line-driven company as I always have been saying in my previous interactions. And my EBITDA and profit, you should see a healthy growth vis-a-vis '23-'24.

items.statement: Management targets defending consolidated EBITDA margins near 27% and PAT margins near 20% achieved in Q4 FY24, though acknowledges it will be tough.
items.quote: In terms of Margins, yes, we will try to defend them or protect them to as close to these levels as possible.

items.statement: Order book stood at INR 5,700 crore as of 31 March 2024, comprising INR 2,600 crore consultancy, INR 2,500 crore turnkey, INR 300 crore export (Mozambique), and INR 300 crore leasing and subsidiary.
items.quote: The order book as of 31st March is INR5,700 crore. Consultancy is INR2,600 crore. Turnkey is INR2,500 crore. Export is the order of Mozambique, which is about INR300 crore, and the balance leasing and subsidiary, et cetera, is INR300 crore.

items.statement: Bangladesh export order of INR 915 crore for 200 coaches signed in April 2024, not included in March order book; revenue expected to start by Q3-Q4 FY25.
items.quote: The INR915 crore order of Bangladesh came in April. So we have not added that to the order book. But now that's also a finite order and a contract agreement has also been signed.

items.statement: Capex will remain in the range of INR 100-140 crore annually, consistent with low capex business model.
items.quote: Two, we are a low capex company. Our capex will always be in the range of INR100-odd crore, INR130 crore to INR140 crore, as you see from the trend.

items.statement: Dividend payout ratio was 95.2% for FY24; management commits to continue returning best to shareholders as EBITDA and PAT grow.
items.quote: Our dividend payout ratio has been 95.2% for FY24. And as we grow and as we aim to grow in both our EBITDA PAT, we will continue to give our best to our shareholders.

items.statement: Order inflow momentum improved to one order per day in Q3 and Q4 FY24, with 100+ orders worth INR 940 crore in Q4; management targets maintaining this rate in FY25.
items.quote: We got 100-plus orders totaling to INR940 crore. And the way the trend is, these orders both export and consultancy orders, which we have been getting across sectors, I think we are confident that the FY24, which is a year of consolidation.

items.statement: Two export orders won after 4-year gap: INR 300 crore for 10 locomotives from Mozambique and INR 915 crore for 200 coaches from Bangladesh; both global tenders with tighter margins.
items.quote: These 2 orders in the last few months, INR300 crore plus and INR900 crore is a good step after a gap of 4-plus years. This INR900 crore from Bangladesh is for 200 coaches and INR300 crore from Mozambique, is for 10 locomotives.

items.statement: Export margins on new global tender orders will be much tighter than historical 20-25% range; management aims to optimize execution to improve margins.
items.quote: But fact that getting these orders on global tenders, the margins will be much, much tighter than the erstwhile export margins, which were in the range of 20%, 25%.

items.statement: Quality Assurance business client mix flipped from 2/3 Indian Railways to over 50% non-IR clients by end of FY24, with orders from defence, power, urban infra, PM Vishwakarma (INR 67 crore) and GeM portal (INR 14-15 crore).
items.quote: By the end of Q4, it has changed over that more than 50% to 55% is non-IR clients. We have got some interesting orders across spectrum, whether it is defence, whether it is power distribution, discoms, whether it is the sewage or urban infra or water or PM Vishwakarma quality checks order of INR 67 crore for the tool kits being supplied.

items.statement: Consultancy revenue (consolidated) reached all-time high of INR 1,300 crore in FY24, up 10% year-on-year in project consultancy.
items.quote: In fact, the total consultancy revenue (consolidated) reached a figure of about INR1,300 crore, which is an all-time high, which was a huge satisfaction to us because it is moving in the right trend and could help minimize the impact of the 2 challenges.

items.statement: Bangladesh coach order (200 coaches, 8 types) to start prototype production in a month; revenue realization targeted by Q3-Q4 FY25. Locomotive order (10 units) longer cycle, revenue may slip to early FY26.
items.quote: We recently on 20th May signed the formal contract agreement also. So now the final designs and approvals are underway and we will start production of the prototype and manufacturing very soon in a month or so.

items.statement: Turnkey order book of INR 2,500 crore executable over roughly 2.5-3 years; fresh turnkey orders limited to ~INR 500 crore in FY24.
items.quote: See, Tunrkey, by nature on average take about 2.5 to 3 years on an average. Some may take more. We are taking a limited turnkey projects. In fact, if you see the fresh orders in our turnkey have been only in the range of about INR500-odd crore in the last FY.

items.statement: Turnkey margins range 3-4%; consultancy margins ~45% in Q4 but under pressure from competitive bidding in both project consultancy and QA.
items.quote: Turnkey business by nature have a margin ranging from 3% to 4%.

items.statement: Management claims RITES is the only Indian company with full-spectrum infrastructure consultancy across 13 verticals (airports, ports, highways, metros, rail, buildings, etc.) under one roof.
items.quote: Interestingly, we can say with confidence that in the infrastructure consultancy business, we are maybe the only Indian company, whether in the PSU space or private space, which has all areas of infrastructure consultancy, except maybe oil and natural gas under one roof.

items.statement: Leasing business seeing growing client base across private and public sectors (power, cement, ports, steel); competition increasing but management targets higher revenue and EBITDA.
items.quote: Number of new clients, both in the private and public sector have been approaching us. And we are moving in the right direction in expanding our client base in the leasing business.

items.statement: REMC (subsidiary) signed first PPA for 900 MW round-the-clock tender, second LOA for 700 MW issued; solar plant at Bhilai inaugurated; revenue up 30%+, PAT up 37%+, dividend ~INR 80 crore (51% to RITES).
items.quote: The first PPA of 900 megawatts was signed. The second LOA for 700 megawatts RTC tenders is issued. There have been initiatives under the solar power plant Bhilai getting inaugurated under the developer mode.

items.statement: Shift from nomination to competitive bidding across consultancy and export orders compressing margins; management focuses on cost optimization and faster execution to protect profitability.
items.quote: The change, which happened about 2.5 years back in terms of nomination vis-a-vis competitive mode. That is the major change, which has been there for about 2, 2.5 years.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free; business model emphasizes low capex, no construction risk, and bottom-line focus.
items.quote: One, we are a debt-free company. Two, we are a low capex company. Our capex will always be in the range of INR100-odd crore, INR130 crore to INR140 crore, as you see from the trend. Three, we are not going to be a construction company.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue projected at Rs. 2,000 crore in FY25, approximately 2x growth from FY24.
items.quote: In FY '25, on a consolidated basis, Gensol is projected to achieve the milestone of Rs. 2,000 crore revenue, approximately 2x growth from what we did in FY '24.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margins expected to remain at 25%-26%.
items.quote: So, I think on the bottom line, we have said that our consolidated EBITDA margins are about 25%-26% We see that we should continue to do the similar kind of numbers.

items.statement: EV manufacturing revenue expected between Rs. 50 and Rs. 100 crores in FY25.
items.quote: And in terms of revenue, we are expecting that we will have a revenue of between Rs. 50 and Rs. 100 crores from EV manufacturing in FY '25.

items.statement: Scorpius Trackers revenue expected to double between FY24 and FY25.
items.quote: The Scorpius Tracker, the revenue from there is expected to actually double between FY '24 and FY '25.

items.statement: Solar order book stands at Rs. 1,448 crores as of FY24 end.
items.quote: Our solar order book stands at Rs. 1,448 crores as on FY '24 end with a big pipeline that far surpasses the number.

items.statement: Scorpius Trackers order book approximately Rs. 100 crores out of total Rs. 1,700 crores.
items.quote: I would not have the exact number, but I can today tell you that approximately out of the Rs. 1,700 crore order books, Scorpius would have about a Rs. 100 crore-ish order book.

items.statement: EV manufacturing plant requires additional CAPEX of Rs. 75-100 crores.
items.quote: think on the EV manufacturing side, it will need between Rs. 75 and 100 crores more and if the EV leasing book will continue to grow by 100% year-on-year

items.statement: India to have over 300 GW solar power by FY30, ensuring no dearth of orders.
items.quote: I think we are seeing that India is going to have some 300 plus gigawatt of solar power by FY '30, which means that there is going to be no dearth of orders for solar, no dearth of orders for battery energy storage systems.

items.statement: EV leasing and solar businesses each expected to contribute half of EBITDA next year.
items.quote: Half of the EBITDA next year will come from the EV leasing business and half of the EBITDA will come from the solar business.

items.statement: Promoter pledges for IREDA and PFC to remain for 2-3 years; some pledges may reduce in six months.
items.quote: So, I think the pledge from IREDA, PFC will only happen at the end of the duration of the debt, which might be between two and three years from the loan that we have taken for investment into promoter, that we have taken to invest in the warrants round. I think that you could see the pledge coming down in about six months' time.

items.statement: Rs. 900 crores fund raise to open in early June; money expected from June.
items.quote: We are going to open up o ur round in the early part of June is when we are going to open up the round. So, there is, we have still not taken the equity

items.statement: EV leasing cost of funds 10%-10.5%, lease cost 14%-15%.
items.quote: One stream of income is the income that we get, which is purely what I can say is the arbitrage which we have, where our cost of funds is between 10%-10.5%, whereas the lease cost is computed at between 14% and 15%.

items.statement: EV leasing book is pristine with no payment delays.
items.quote: But as of even yesterday, I can confirm to you that not even one customer has delayed any payment by even one day on the EV leasing side.

items.statement: Monthly outgo expected to be around Rs. 150 crores this year.
items.quote: So, we are making very prudent decisions when it comes to our treasury operations and hence, you will continue to see that while we maintain our monthly outgo for this particular year is going to be in the range of Rs. 150 crores a month.

items.statement: Net debt-to-equity is 2.7, expected to reduce with fund raise.
items.quote: So, our net debt-to-equity is actually 2.7, because the company had about close to Rs. 400 crores plus cash, which was there. Hence, you have to not look at the debt-to-equity, but the net debt-to-equity.

items.statement: Current order book is INR38,000 crores including INR11,216 crores destroyer, INR17,000 crores frigates, INR3,000 crores submarine, INR3,000 crores coast guard, INR2,000 crores MRLS, INR350 crores export, INR1,000-1,500 crores others
items.quote: MRLs, medium refit and life certification INR2000 crores, exports INR350 crores and others approximately INR1000 crores to INR1500 crores, total INR38,000 crores.

items.statement: FY25 targeting three deliveries: one destroyer, one frigate, one submarine; FY25 likely peak revenue on current order book; two frigates possible if plan holds

items.statement: Expects total revenue of about INR2,500 crores in FY25.
items.quote: We expect to record total revenue of about INR2,500 crores in financial year '25.

items.statement: Total order book including SPVs and GIC platform surpassed INR21,000 crores.
items.quote: Our total order book, including all SPVs and GIC platform h as surpassed INR 21,000 crores on date, indicating a promising outlook for future revenue

items.statement: L1 status in projects around INR11,000 crores.
items.quote: Currently, we have L1 in projects -- but exact number, will be around INR11,000 crores.

items.statement: Expects 60-70 million smart meters installed in India this financial year.
items.quote: In this financial year, I personally believe that at least 60 million to 70 million smart meters will be installed.

items.statement: Realistic assumption for 25 crore smart meters target is next four to five years.
items.quote: My realistic assumption will be it will happen in next four to five years.

items.statement: Out of INR19,000 crores platform orders, 75-80% will come back to Genus; of that, 50% supply, 20% installation, 30% O&M.
items.quote: Out of this INR19,000 crores, 80% will come to Genus. And this 80% if you form let's make this 80% at 100%. So then 50% of that 100% would be of supply around 20% will be installation and aro und 30% will be O&M, operation and maintenance

items.statement: O&M margins are comparatively better than supply and installation.
items.quote: in terms of margins definitely, O&M is comparatively better than by supply installation.

items.statement: Adding capacity at Guwahati plant to reach 1.5 crores electronic meters per year.
items.quote: we are adding up some capacity now Guwahati plant. So we will reach to a comfortable level of INR1.5 crores electronic meters every year.

items.statement: Exports expected to be at least INR150 crores this year.
items.quote: Last year also, we did exports of more than INR100 crores, and this year also, we expect to do at least INR150 crores.

items.statement: Working capital intensity to continue for next 6-12 months, then improve.
items.quote: Next 6-12 months, I continue to see that because long projects will come on the ground, FAT/SAT will open and then money will start soon. But next year onwards, I definitely see the working capital intensity getting better for Genus.

items.statement: Bank guarantee exposure more than INR600-700 crores.
items.quote: we have an exposure of more than INR600 -INR700 crores in terms of the bank guarantee.

items.statement: Gas meters opportunity 8-10 crores sold in next 7-8 years.
items.quote: we can see some 8 crores to 10 crores gas meters should be sold in like 7 to 8 years.

items.statement: Smart gas meter price around INR3,000 to INR3,500.
items.quote: And smart gas meter is around INR3,000 to INR3,500.

items.statement: Export margins are better than Indian margins for hardware.
items.quote: Export margins are comparatively better than the Indian margins for hardware.

items.statement: Management targets 30% to 40% consolidated growth for FY25.
items.quote: We are looking at around 30% to 40% growth this financial year.

items.statement: FrogData targeted to grow 100%, but 75-80% growth seen as quite possible.
items.quote: Yes, I mean, we are targeting for 100. We have hired a lot of new salespeople. We are also expanding our geographical reach in the U.S. So , we are targeting 100%, but I think that 75% to 80% growth is quite possible.

items.statement: Internal target to reach 500-crore turnover in three years.
items.quote: See, our internal projections or our internal target in the next three years is to try and reach a 500-crore turnover. It's very, very aggressive. I agree. That's our internal target.

items.statement: Margins expected to improve or remain same as costs stay flat.
items.quote: Yes, because our costs will remain quite flat. So, our margin should actually improve, if not remain the same. We don't expect much of cost expansion in the current year.

items.statement: FrogData has 30-40% margin and pricing increase to drive uptick.
items.quote: We have around 30% to 40% margin in FrogData and we have actually this year increasing pricing on that. So, we should see an uptick on the margins in FrogData business because based on the benefit the dealers are getting, we have decided to increase pricing because I think the market can bear it.

items.statement: Planning to raise funds by divesting 10-15% stake in FrogData at $60-80 million valuation.
items.quote: We are looking at between 10% to 15% and the valuation we are trying to achieve is between 60 to 80 million for the business.

items.statement: Fundraise for FrogData expected to close by end of this calendar year.
items.quote: I would say latest before December this year, definitely, worst case.

items.statement: R&D expenses to remain constant in absolute terms, but fall as percentage of revenue.
items.quote: R&D is always constant, because we keep wo rking on new products, because we are always planning what is going to be relevant five years from today or three years or even 10 years from today. Being a product company, I need to continue investing in new development.

items.statement: FrogData share of revenue increased to 26% and will contribute significantly to top and bottom line.
items.quote: See, over the last three years FrogData share has been increasing. So, in current FY, it's already 26%. Three years back it was hardly a single digit. So, it will contribute significantly to the top line and more significantly to the bottom line going forward.

items.statement: Expects $1 million+ from Stellantis Europe CRM rollout this year.

items.statement: Spain expected to generate at least couple of million euros, Germany 4-5 million euros annually once operational.

items.quote: Spain should be at least couple of million euros. Germany should be more, 4-5 million euros a year. Once they are fully operational and there is enough people know about us.

items.statement: Tax rate to remain same for two years, then normalize to 25% in FY27.
items.quote: I think it will remain the same. I think only by '26-'27, you start seeing a higher tax rate coming in, kicking in.

items.statement: VR product expected to be ready for market by end of this financial year.
items.quote: We are working on it. There is still some challenges there So, I think by end of this financial year, we should have a product ready for the market.

items.statement: Entering Germany this year, focusing on Germany and Spain for expansion.
items.quote: We are seriously entering Germany this year. We have already entered Spain. Last year, we are increasing our presence there. So, Europe will be a major thrust because there is a huge potential out there, especially for digital.

items.statement: FrogData fundraise to be used for US sales and tech team expansion.
items.quote: It will be used in the U.S. for sales expansion and expansion of the tech team.

items.quote: With our existing product, we have a good market share in some of the regulatory markets and going forward, I think few more regulatory markets are opening up from the patent opportunity. items.statement: R&D split: ~40% on cost optimization/backward integration, ~60% on new/niche products; prioritization based on patent expiries and customer inquiries

items.quote: We had a slightly slow year last year; 2.5% revenue growth is not spectacular, but we hope that with the scaling up of our sales engine across the t hree major geographies, our growth in the coming year will be much better than it was last year

items.statement: South Africa operations to start in Q2 or Q3 FY2024 with a center in Cape Town.
items.quote: We expect to start operations in either Q2 FY2024 or Q3 FY2024 with a center in Cape Town, and we are expecting to be able to support clients, primarily from the UK, North America, and Australia from Cape Town.

items.statement: Colombia center is almost full with about 200 people working there.

items.statement: Digital services share of revenues expected to grow organically and inorganically.
items.quote: So, that is the current mix, and we expect that the digital services as a percentage of revenues, are going to grow both organically and inorganically.

items.statement: Share of labor arbitrage driven services will go down as more transformative solutions are implemented.
items.quote: You will find that our share of only labor arbitrage driven services will go down as we implement more transformative solutions around Gen AI, artificial intelligence, and the new technologies such as cybersecurity and all of that.

items.statement: Net cash and treasury surplus to be used for organic growth and strategic acquisitions.
items.quote: So, it is going to be used as a combination for organic growth as well as for acquisitions, which will be strategic in nature and add to our overall capabilities and offerings.

items.statement: Digital television subscriber base grew by just over 8% year-on-year to about 4.43 million.
items.quote: And we have seen traction on that as well, with the base growing by just over 8% year-on-year to about 4.43 million.

items.quote: The industry level we know is significant double digits annually, in the low 20s or mid 20s annually, and we have been able to buck the trend and literally half that.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA grew 45.8% in FY2024.

items.quote: Operating EBITDA has improved close to 46% on year-on-year basis and at the overall level, our Operating EBITDA margins have expanded again significantly from 5.4% (FY2023) to 7.7% (FY2024).

items.statement: Received claim amount of INR135 crores principal and INR109 crores interest in Q4 FY24.
items.quote: During the year Q4 FY24, the company received a claim amount of INR135 crores towards principal and INR109 crores towards interest, which were shown in the revenue and other income respectively.

items.statement: HAM projects fiscal progress as of March 31, 2024: Magadi-Somwarpet 83%, Oddanchatram-Madathukulam 99%, Ramanattukara-Valanchery 73%, Valanchery-Kappirikkad 75%, Chittor-Thatchur 51%.
