items.quote: Yes. So there are three projects that we are due to receive our work order. One is the Tanzania, it is around INR50 crores assignment. There is one project in Mozambique and one project in Ghana.

items.statement: Employees added continuously via in-house recruitment; consent taken during bidding; key professionals pre-identified for international projects
items.quote: So when it comes to recruitment, first, we have to take their consent while bidding. So during submission of bids itself, we have to take the consent and as and when the project is awarded, the employees are taken on the roles.

items.statement: FY24 total income INR82.41 crores, up 0.13% YoY; EBITDA INR14.75 crores, up 43% YoY; PAT INR5.89 crores, up 22.77% YoY
items.quote: For the full fiscal year 2024, the company achieved a total income of INR82.41 crores, a slight year-on-year growth of 0.13%. items.statement: Election cycles cause order delays every 5 years; international diversification aims to mitigate this dependency
items.quote: This -- as I said that this mainly happened due to the elections that were due at the central government level. And this is a trend that is there every 5 years. Hence, now with international orders coming up, we will be able to mitigate this sector. There is no dependency on the central government elections.

items.statement: Expects 40-50% year-on-year growth for next couple of years.
items.quote: So growth, we are looking to continue the current growth trend of 40% to 50% year-on-year for the next couple of years. I mean, 40% on a conservative level, we are hoping to grow for the next couple of years.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin of 8.5-9.5% for current financial year.
items.quote: And, as far as EBITDA is concerned, we are expecting EBITDA to be in the range of 8.5% to 9%, 9.5% for the current financial year.

items.statement: Plans to increase ODU capacity by 20% in coming year due to demand.
items.quote: We are also looking at increasing our capacity by about 20% in ODU in the coming year, because of increased demand.

items.statement: Expects 50-70% capacity utilisation in commercial refrigeration next year.
items.quote: And we hope that by next year, we will reach a capacity utilisation of 50% to 70% of the capacity that we're creating this year.

items.statement: Expects PAT margin of 2-3% depending on depreciation method.
items.quote: So PAT between 2% and 3%, we are contemplating if depreciation if you want to go into a straight line depreciation calculation, then PAT will go towards 3%, maybe slightly higher. But if we continue WDV, then about 2%.

items.statement: Plans to start Chennai unit for AC components in current financial year.
items.quote: This year, we also plan to start a unit in Chennai for making components for air conditioners, because some of our customers are wanting us to make certain parts locally for them in Chennai. So our unit in Chennai is also planned in the current financial year.

items.statement: May enter washing machine segment towards end of year or next year.
items.period: end of this year or next year
items.quote: We are also exploring washing machine as a segment. So we might enter washing machine also either towards the end of this year or maybe next year, but it is not confirmed as of yet.

items.statement: Expects June quarter to be better than last year.
items.quote: So, April and May normally is good every year. And this year, June is also looking to be really good, which is not normally the case because June onwards, the sales start declining. items.statement: Expects ODU to pressure EBITDA, but other verticals to balance.
items.quote: So EBITDA with ODU is lower than IDU, because the value addition in the overall product is lower. So ODU is expected to put pressure on EBITDA, but I think the other verticals like commercial ref we'll probably balance it out slightly.

items.statement: Pricing with customers reset quarterly based on LME average.

items.statement: Interest cost expected to be lower or similar this year despite growth.
items.quote: So with the recent fundraise that we did, we believe this year, the interest cost will be slightly lower than last year even after the growth coming in. So it will be similar or a lower number, irrespective of the growth.

items.statement: Plans to use QIP proceeds for working capital and capex.
items.quote: So, working capital and CapEx primarily.

items.statement: Expects 2-3% of sales from exports this year.
items.quote: And I think this year our export number is, we are expecting at least 2%, 3% of our sales to come from export. And if that happens, we'll continue to build on it in the coming years.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 15-20% YoY for next 2-3 years
items.quote: Our vision endeavor will be continuing this trajectory of growth 15% to 20% Y-on-Y that should be our endeavor and the guidance for the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of around 3%+ in 1-2 years
items.quote: Range we should be hovering around 3 plus percent in year or two to come.

items.statement: Rs 1000 crore revenue target remains on horizon, halfway there currently
items.quote: The Rs. 1000 crore mark still stays on the horizon. And if you say how close , we are halfway there.

items.statement: FY26 aspirational target for Rs 1000 crore revenue
items.quote: FY26 would be my dream target , but our endeavor is there.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 4.36%, up 43 bps YoY
items.quote: EBITDA margins stood at 4.36%, an improvement of 43 bps compared to the previous year.

items.statement: Full year FY24 net profit margin 2.53%
items.quote: Net profit for the margin stood at 2.53%.

items.statement: Segment margins: Networking 5-7%, UC 7-9%, Security double-digit
items.quote: The margins in the networking patch, what we call it, is a round hovering around 5 % to 7%. In the UC patch, it is approximately 7% to 8% or 9% and in the security patch, it is double digit.

items.statement: Margins improving via scale, efficiency, services attachment, and product mix optimization
items.quote: as the scale increases and we continue to bring efficiency into our operations and thirdly, the product mix of adding services to the products which we are getting and more and more solutions offering as we grow, we see that the margins improv ing to a better level than this

items.statement: Strong demand for Samsung, NETSCOUT, Netgear, D-Link, Arbor products and software/services in FY24
items.quote: due to strong demand in our products like Samsung, NETSCOUT, Netgear, D-Link, Arbor and other software and services.

items.statement: Interactive panel revenue expected Rs 30-50 crore in FY25 vs Rs 8-12 crore in FY24
items.quote: we see that contributing to a decent maybe Rs. 30 to Rs. 50 crores this year interactive panel into our kitty.

items.statement: Enterprise security fastest growing segment, now ~25% of revenue
items.quote: enterprise security business, which is the latest addition and as the time goes, it has a more and more demand has risen to approximately 25% of our kitty.

items.statement: Order book not relevant; quoted funnel ~Rs 40-50 crore converting in month/quarter
items.quote: It is approx imately around Rs. 40 crores to Rs. 50 crores which we are already quoted, and the order should be coming through maybe in this month or the quarter next, so order book is not very relevant to our business.

items.statement: Revenue mix: Networking 45-50%, UC 25-30%, Enterprise Security ~25%
items.quote: networking. So networkin g still remains a huge chunk of our business, which is approximately 45%-50% of our business, the unified communication patch also contributes around 25 %-30% of our business and the enterprise security business

items.statement: Hardware 80%, Software/Services 20% of FY24 revenue
items.quote: FY24, hardware is 80%, 20% comes from the software services.

items.statement: Top 15 customers contribute 40-50% of revenue; key accounts include Tata Communications, Hitachi, NSE/BSE via SI partners
items.quote: our top 15 of them will be contributing around 40%-50% of our business.

items.statement: Samsung contributes 15-20% of UC revenue; Netgear 45-50% of Networking; NETSCOUT/Arbor 60% of Security
items.quote: Samsung would be around 15% to 20% contributing out of that. So that answers. The third enterprise security, NETSCOUT and Arbor are visibility solutions and DDoS security solutions is 60% of that patch which we offer.

items.statement: No direct listed peer with same 3-domain mix; differentiated by solution/services vs pure distribution
items.quote: We are working into three domains, so there is no apple-to-apple company which is available exactly in these domains.

items.statement: Expanded operations to South India this year; overseas expansion under study
items.quote: This year, we have just moved to the southern India, which we are not present. So we just set up our operations in Southern India, the team is in place.

items.statement: Open to raising funds via bank debt or preferential issue as business demands to fuel growth
items.quote: if need be, as the business demands, we are open to raising more funds from bank or maybe via preference or whatever the board feels right, we may raise.

items.statement: Promoters not diluting stake; warrants conversion will restore promoter holding
items.quote: promoters are not in the mode of diluting the stake. We have done a preferential thing, but parallelly, there has been warrants which are convertible, which has been issued which will be up on conversion of warrants will be again back to what we were

items.statement: ~70 employees across sales, engineering, technical support, finance, admin; no in-house software development
items.quote: We are approximately 70 plus team and it is mixture of everything. It is not only sales, sales support guys, the engineer, the technician and obviously the finance and the admin team.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 revenue Rs 154.59 crore, up 60.74% YoY
items.quote: have reported Rs. 154.59 crores of revenue during Q4 of FY 24, a 60.74% Y-on-Y rise

items.statement: FY24 revenue Rs 459.63 crore, up 27.81% YoY
items.quote: we have reported Rs. 459.63 crores revenue in FY24, a 27.81% year -on-year rise

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA Rs 6.74 crore, up 78.16% YoY
items.quote: Our EBITDA for the fourth quarter stands at Rs. 6.74 crores, increasing 78.16% Y-on-Y

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA Rs 20.04 crore, up 57.53% YoY

items.statement: FY24 net profit Rs 11.61 crore vs Rs 7.08 crore in FY23
items.quote: Our net profits during the full year is Rs. 11.61 crore against profit of Rs. 7.08 crore in FY23.

items.statement: Security segment quarterly spike due to Diwali deferrals; may not repeat every quarter
items.quote: some orders which were supposed to be executed in OND because of that Diwali patch, they got pushed into the JFM quarter and because of that JFM quarter, you see a big spike. This kind of numbers would may not be the same

items.statement: Management expects to maintain historic revenue growth of 15% to 20%.
items.quote: Will grow accordingly on our regular previous year ’s growth and we don’t do bi dding very aggressively. We maintain it so that we can execute projects on time and give quality work, so we hope that we can maintain our historic increase of 15% to 20

items.statement: EBITDA margins will be sustained at around 13% to 14%.
items.quote: Gradually we have grown and we will sustain our margins at around 13% to 14%.

items.statement: Current order book stands at around Rs. 4,717 crores to be executed over 24 to 36 months.

items.statement: Aim to maintain order book to turnover ratio around 3 times.

items.statement: No immediate need for capex as adequate equipment is available.
items.quote: No, as of now we have proper equipment, so we hope that with this equipment itself new projects can be done and if any specific equipment is required then we can procure that.

items.statement: Government focus on infrastructure is good and bidding is continuous.

items.statement: Diversifying across states; Rajasthan portion of order book reduced from 68% to 37%.
items.quote: Yes, sir. We are diversifying in other states also if we compare our last order book, in that our Rajasthan portion in that it came from 68% to 37% now and in other states its revenue has gone to higher side.

items.statement: Debt equity ratio will be maintained under one.

items.statement: Historic bidding success ratio is around 17%.

items.statement: Mobilization advances on balance sheet were around Rs. 61 crores.

items.statement: Finance cost will be in line with revenue growth.

items.statement: No significant impact from elections or summer on execution.

items.statement: Focus on railways and roads for expansion.

items.statement: Finance charge on lease asset to reduce to INR3.11 crores in FY24-25.

items.statement: Material cost reduction impact to be fully visible in Q1 and Q2.
items.quote: The full impact of that will be visible in Q1 and Q2.

items.statement: AC volumes in April and May more than 100,000 units.

items.statement: Growth in ACs to come from brand sales, not OEM.
items.quote: The growth this year will come from brand sales, not so much from OEM sales.

items.statement: Supply chain issues with compressors impacted Q4 and April-May.
items.quote: Basically, we - the one major item which we have, which is the compressors, which are being imported, we ran short. And we also ran short in April, May.

items.statement: No immediate price hikes; decision after June 15.
items.quote: So, what he said was that he is going to decide on this after 15th of June. So, we'll stick with that. We'll see how it goes and then we'll take the call. As of now, we are not under pressure per se.

items.statement: AC capacity is 500,000 units, working on increasing it.
items.quote: See, our capacity currently is 500,000 ACs with an assembly line running in single shift and some of the feeder lines running in two shifts. And we are working on increasing it in line with what we require.

items.statement: Will not do M&A until cash reaches INR500 crores.
items.quote: As we've said in the investor call, we will not do anything until the cash moves up to over INRS500 crores.

items.statement: Refrigerator breakeven at 35,000-37,000 units per month.
items.quote: So to reach breakeven, IFB Refrigeration Limited needs to do roughly about 35,000 to 37,000 refrigerators a month.

items.statement: Growth expected around 15% on average for FY25.
items.quote: But, as we discussed catlier also, the growth will not be very aggressive in the sense of, anywhere between, you can say on an average, maybe 15%. That would be a good growth as far as we are concerned

items.statement: Total capex INR12-15 crores including new facility and automation.
items.quote: So with all this, everything, it could be around INR12 crores to INR1S crores, which would include everywhere, the existing facilitics as well as the new facility

items.statement: New Bangalore facility capex INR7-8 crores, under INR10 crores.
items.quote: New facility, this total maybe INR7 crores, INRS crores, maybe under INR10 crores of capex in that facility

items.statement: Gross margins expected to remain at current levels.
items.quote: So, yes, gross margins we expect it fo remain in these levels. And those are the types of businesses that we are looking at

items.statement: Export margins better than domestic by 4-5%.
items.quote: Yes, the margins are better than the, domestic customers basically by 4% or 5%ive percent

items.statement: Export business to grow significantly after Q3.
items.quote: As far as exports are concerned, which is very low as of today, only single digit numbers, we have three large customers for export, one from Australia and two from United States and two of them, we have already started supplics and commercial orders are in place and this business should go up significantly after the third quarter onwards

items.statement: Construction equipment share to rise, electricals share to fall.
items.quote: So, maybe the percentage of sale to clectricals will go down as compared to the past, this year ended March '24. And construction equipment percentage may go up slightly

items.statement: Skilled manpower shortage and rising employee costs are concerns.
items.quote: So in that area, I see, there is one arca of concern, which I scc, because one is the lack of skilled manpower availability in this country

items.statement: Difficulty in adding new large customers domestically.
items.quote: But I'n not finding that we are definitely struggling to add customers to our profile. So, we can grow at that pace. If we want to grow at 20% or 20% plus, then the only way to do that is o add customers to what we have. And that part is proving to be very difficult

items.statement: Growth funded by internal accruals and some debt, equity only if large opportunity.
items.quote: So going forward also at least in the coming year a good part of growth whatever we have planned will be out of internal aceruals. There will be some loan requirements also

items.statement: Revenue potential INR250-300 crores from current and upcoming facilities.
items.quote: So with this, new facility in place and all the existing setup, actually, with balancing cquipment and people and all that, it can be scaled up very substantially from here in the sense of, INR250 crores, INR300 crores business the whole company can do with this kind of facility

items.statement: Exports could reach 40-50% of revenue in about three years.
items.quote: It is difficult for me to say, I would say about three years is what I

items.statement: Management will not provide forward guidance on growth or margins
items.quote: No, we will not be doing any forward guidance.

items.statement: Global outbound travel expected to fully recover by end of 2024 and reach $2.7 trillion by 2027
items.quote: Post COVID, revival in outbound travel has been strong and full recovery is expected by the end of this year. Historically, outbound travel has grown at a pace of 5-6% every year. So, global travel spend is expected to reach nearly US $2.7 trillion by the year 2027.

items.statement: India outbound travel spending surged 24% to $17 billion in FY24 with 8-11% projected air passenger growth
items.quote: Overseas travel spending has surged to US $17 billion in this last financial year, marking a notable 24% increase over the previous year. Projections indicate an anticipated growth in international air passenger traffic by 8% to 11%.

items.statement: Monthly transacting buyers outside India grew 20% driving 31% international GTV growth; enterprise buyers grew 8% driving 19% overall GTV growth
items.quote: Our monthly transacting buyers outside of India grew by around 20%, which led to a growth of 31% in GTV in our international business. At an enterprise level, our monthly transacting buyer base grew by 8%, which led to an overall increase in GTV by 19%.

items.statement: Air take rate steady state at 2.5%; air gross profit expected between 1.2-1.5%
items.quote: So, considering the current situation, we believe that 2.5% should be a steady state growth or the take rate number for air business and similarly, for the gross profit numbers, we expect to maintain it between 1.5% to 1.2%.

items.statement: Significant investment planned in technology and data teams; costs will increase going forward
items.quote: No. I think there is no cost optimization possible, Pratyush, and tech resources remain expensive. So, our significant investment will continue to go into building out the technology and data teams. From the perspective of how we should look at this going forward, we do intend to increase the number of people in the tech team. So, you will see some increase in costs on those heads going forward.

items.statement: 26,500 monthly transacting buyers total with 18,500 in India; international buyers grew 20% vs 8% enterprise growth due to India base effect
items.quote: In fact, in 2024, out of roughly 26,500 buyers, 18,500 are sitting in India. So, while that number has grown, that number is growing at a slow percentage because of the base effect. So, hence the enterprise growth number looks lesser.

items.statement: 85-90% of international business naturally hedged in USD/GBP/EUR; India hotel payments hedged via forwards; airline payments in INR
items.quote: In our international business, a majority of our business is naturally hedged because we are selling in so many countries and buying from so many countries from different suppliers. So let us say, for example, selling in USD and also collecting in USD and making payment to suppliers in USD. So, around 85%-90% of my business in currencies like USD, GBP and Europe in naturally hedged.

items.statement: Working capital remains negative; trade receivables and payables increased due to Jumbonline consolidation and hotel mix with longer booking window
items.quote: Notably, our working capital continues to remain negative. As of March end 2024, there has been a substantial increase in trade receivables and trade payables amount as compared to the past year. This has been primarily due to consolidation of financial numbers of our new acquisition Jumbonline as well as due to the increase in the overall mix of hotel business.

items.statement: IPO raised INR 1,550 Cr total with INR 400 Cr primary infusion for future growth goals
items.quote: The total size of the IPO was INR 1,550 Crore, with INR 400 Crore being the primary infusion of capital. This capital injection will enable us to fulfill our funding requirements to achieve our future goals.

items.statement: Completed 4 acquisitions in 5 years including Jumbonline for Southern European beach hotels; acquisition thesis focuses on adding buyer base or supply base globally
items.quote: Over the last 5 years, we have completed 4 acquisitions, enhancing our global reach and market position. Most recently, we had acquired Jumbonline, which is an aggregator of Southern European Beach Hotel supply. We will continue to look for more opportunities for inorganic growth.

items.statement: Jumbonline contributed INR 36 Cr revenue and INR 3.5 Cr PAT in FY24; material impact expected in coming year
items.quote: So, Swapnil, there was only INR 36 Crore of revenue that was contributed by Jumbo in the last FY numbers. So, we will see some material impact in the Jumbonline in the coming year, but it was not very material for last year. In terms of PAT, the contribution was about INR 3.5 Crore from the Jumbonline business.

items.statement: SG&A at 2.5% of GTV with 0.5% variable (hosting, payment gateway) and 2% fixed; operating leverage expected long-term
items.quote: So, the SG&A cost is at around 2.5%. Two components in the SG&A cost, which is hosting and bandwidth as well as the payment gateway cost, which is prima facie semi-variable or variable in nature basically, which will grow in line most probably with the growth of GTV or the revenue. This amount currently contributes around 0.5%. So, out of the 2.5% of the SG&A, 2% is primarily fixed, and that is wh

items.statement: UAE corporate tax of 9% effective current financial year will increase overall effective tax rate
items.quote: With respect to the tax rates basically, so currently we were not having any taxes for our international business in Dubai or UAE, but from the current financial year, those profits would get taxed at a rate of 9%. So, our overall effective tax rate would increase from what currently we are having.

items.statement: Travel volatility from macroeconomic and political events is fundamental risk; global diversification provides some hedge
items.quote: Travel is highly volatile. It doesn't take long for travel to be doing well and then some global macro event to happen and disrupt travel. So, that is definitely a risk. We are also exposed to a very global travel industry. So the chances of something going wrong in some part of the world is always there, though it also adds a hedge for us because we are not overly concentrated in a certain market

items.statement: Gross profit as percentage of GTV improved to 3.47% from 3.28%; EBITDA grows faster than gross profit due to operating leverage
items.quote: Gross profit as a percentage of GTV for the full year improved to 3.47% from 3.28% last year. EBITDA grows faster than gross profit because of operating leverage, which is quite well demonstrated this year.

items.statement: Hotels provide differentiated pricing for B2B channel vs OTAs as travel agents package rates with flights and ancillaries
items.quote: Hotels usually provide differentiated pricing for the online channels like OTA and B2B channel like ours because our channels serve different kind of traveler. Typically, a travel agent will package the hotel rate along with the flight and ancillaries and give a package to their end customer, which allows hotels a bit of a flexibility on providing lower rates because those rates don't have to nece

items.statement: Europe structured into three regions with separate leaders; North America platform localization and sales team expansion planned
items.quote: We structure Europe into three different distinct regions because it is so large and important for us and we have three different regional leaders running Europe, in different parts of Europe is a testament to the fact that we have very high hopes from this market. North America is also scaling up nicely. The nature of the market is slightly different from Europe and the rest of the world. So, we

items.statement: Targets ~100% revenue growth in FY25 and ~100-150 bps EBITDA margin improvement
items.quote: So, we are targeting, so basically, when we close the 325 crores right now, we're targeting a good revenue growth of around 100% this year with a good improvement in margin right now is around 5.6%, 5.7%. We target to improve it by 1% this year.

items.statement: Phase II capex of ~₹500 crore covering denim, non-denim, yarn, and air-jet weaving expansion
items.quote: So, basically, so expansion that we're talking about, expansion is coming in denim, that'll enhance the capacity from 1.8 crores to 2.52 crores. It is coming in, basically, it is coming in non-denim of 1.8 crores.

items.statement: Denim capacity rising from 1.8 to 2.52 crore m/yr; non-denim 0 to 1.8 crore m/yr; yarn 21 tpd from Oct 2024; 72 air-jet looms for in-house use
items.quote: Our expansion will lead to increase of capacity of around 72 lakh metres from 1.8 crore metre per annum to 2.52 crore per annum. Expansion in non-denim, so we are entering non-denim segment also right now, which will lead to enhancement of capacity from 0 to 1.8 crore metres per annum.

items.statement: Healthy order book of ~2 months (35 lakh metres) including Marks & Spencer, H&M, Reliance, ZARA and domestic clients
items.quote: We have a healthy order book of around two months. So we have a capacity of 50 lakh metres right now. And along with the developments we have an estimated order book of 35 lakh metres right now with the clients like Marks & Spencer, H&M, and numerous clients like this along with the domestic clients.

items.statement: New brand tie-ups with Reliance and ZARA; 90% repeat order rate; 0% rejection rate since inception
items.quote: We have started working with all these brands recently, and we've tied up with Reliance and ZARA. And these are the few players that we've tied up with and which we can disclose right now. And these are all new players.

items.statement: Export margins ~70-100 bps above domestic; targeting shift from trader (40-50%) to brand/export mix for margin improvement
items.quote: So if a margin in domestic is around 5%, then I'll anyho w achieve more margin of around 0.7% to 1% in exports fabric, if I target the right customers and if I can provide the fabric on time

items.statement: Final stage of obtaining 10-11 certifications (BSI ISO, SA8000, GOTS, GRS, ORS, Worldly) to unlock export markets
items.quote: In textile industry, we will be one of the few companies in India that is in the final stage of obtaining BSI certificates of numerous ISO and SA8000 along with many textile certification that will in total be a certification basket of around 10 to 11 certificates.

items.statement: Yarn booked on order date to pass through raw material cost; best-in-class cotton buying claimed
items.quote: when we sell the fabric to a customer, we take the current rate of the yarn. We book the yarn on the current date, and then we sell the fabric. So we mitigate th e variation of raw material there

items.statement: Interest subsidy expected from next quarter after COD of weaving plants; will reduce finance cost
items.quote: Swaraj will start receiving subsidies after the COD of weaving denim and non-denim plant. So after the commercial production of this plant has started, we hope to start receiving subsidy from the next quarter itself.

items.statement: No long-term volume contracts in textile; orders depend on continuous development and competitive pricing; commodity cycles can compress margins
items.quote: In textile industry, there is no long-term tie up like this. That you have a written tie up of 10 lakh metres per month. There's no long-term tie up in textile industries. It is a job work then. So it all depends on the price variations and all the developments that we're doing.

items.statement: FY25 revenue target of Rs 650-700 crore
items.quote: So the revenue of ₹650 crores to 700 crores.

items.statement: Conservative PAT margin target of 6.5% post expansion
items.quote: No, basically what happened was, if I talk about 6.5%, I'm talking about a conservative side right now.

items.statement: Total project investment around Rs 300 crore including working capital
items.quote: Basically this investment of mine consists of working capital investment too, so the investing is will be around ₹300 crores.

items.statement: Peak term loan debt expected at Rs 220 crore
items.quote: Peak debt number will be around ₹220 crores of term loan.

items.statement: Weaving denim and non-denim expansion completed this month; spinning by October 2024
items.quote: Spinning division, yes. For, weaving, for denim and for non-denim, it will be completed this month itself.

items.statement: Existing denim capacity 1.8 crore metres at 100% utilisation generating Rs 350-380 crore revenue
items.quote: if I talk about 1.8 crores, we have existing capacity of 1.8 crores that is already running at 100% capacity. That can generate the revenue of 350 to 380 crores.

items.statement: Additional capacity of 72 lakh + 1.8 lakh metres; fabric division max capacity Rs 550 crore
items.quote: The additional capacity, if I talk about of 72 lakhs plus 1.8 lakhs, 1.8 crores has a maximum capacity of around 550 crores, the fabric division that I'm talking about.

items.statement: Targeting 60-70% production utilisation in FY25 for new capacity
items.quote: So I'm targeting with this we will be able to achieve roughly 60% to 70% production in this year.

items.statement: Current order book 35 lakh metres, up from 17-20 lakh metres a year ago
items.quote: I think we have an order book of like 35 lakh metres. If I talk about last year at the same time, what would be your order book approximate? Nasir Khan: That time my order book was around 17 lakhs to 20

items.statement: Export order book 5-6 lakh metres; trading 15-17 lakh metres; balance garments and brands
items.quote: Currently, we have an order book of export of 5 lakh metres right now. We have about 5 lakh to 6 lakh metres of exports orders in hand. Now, let's assume that we will have an order book of around 15 lakhs to 17 lakhs of trading.

items.statement: Tied up with Reliance Trends; order book covers two months supply
items.quote: We have tied up with Reliance Trends, which have a very huge brands portfolio right now. We're tied up with Reliance Trends and apart from that, we are not tying up in terms of quantity, but as a tie up in such a way that that company shall give us the first tie up supply the fabric to them in such a way that we already have an order book of two months right now.

items.statement: Target to reduce trader segment by 25%; aim for 25-30% brands, 25-30% exports, 20-25% cutters
items.quote: So we are targeting to reduce the trading segment by 25%. So we'll keep a portfolio of around 20%, 25% of cutters, 25% to 30% of brands, and 25%, 30% of exports, and the rest will be divided into trading.

items.statement: H2 FY24 EBITDA margin 13.5% considered sustainable
items.quote: It is very sustainable for us. Basically I will tell you that when you visit the plant, and the kind of booking you see with us, because defining something in the books is a different thing.

items.statement: EBITDA margin FY24 was 12.43%
items.quote: We did have, it was around, I think the EBITDA margin was 12.43%, I guess.

items.statement: Utility cost reduction example: from Rs 30 to Rs 24 per unit due to shared utilities
items.quote: if I talk about costing is ₹30 right now, then our costing will be reduced ₹24. I'm giving you examples, the utility costing I'm talking about because we have installed the plant in the same utility.

items.statement: Power rate incentives in Rajasthan and MP to save Rs 5.5-6 crore annually at full capacity (1.5 lakh units/day)
items.quote: the power rate that has been offered to us. I'll personally share it with you, but that itself makes a huge difference, because we'll have a consumption of around 1,50,000 units per day after starting of all the plants. And that will impact, that will give us a return of estimatedly , it will make an impact on our balance sheet of minimum 5.5 Cr to 6 Cr, if I compare to the existing units.

items.statement: Job work outsourcing of Rs 18-19 crore last year to be cut by 50% with in-house weaving
items.quote: last year we paid an hour. We did a job work of around 18 to 19 crores of job work we did outside. So that particular job work will be minimised to, I think 50% because the capacity will also increase of us.

items.statement: Total subsidies (capital, interest, power, land) estimated Rs 130-150 crore over 7 years
items.quote: My subsidy will exceed from ₹130 crores to ₹150 crores including interest subsidies, electricity subsidies, capital subsidies that will be directly credited to the account.

items.statement: First subsidy tranche of Rs 10-15 crore expected next quarter
items.quote: I hope that in the next quarter, the initial first tranche of ₹10 - ₹15 crores will be released.

items.statement: Capital subsidy 30% of plant & machinery + building investment, released over 7 years
items.quote: the total investment in plant, machinery and building will be subsidised by 30%. The actual subsidiary that will be released will be around 32%, 33%. But on the conservative side, I'm talking about 30% right now.

items.statement: Interest subsidy 7% on term loan, released quarterly after drawdown schedule
items.quote: Interest side, if I talk about so, basically if I say ₹200 crores of loan is my loan, then you can calculate 7% on ₹200 crores. After preparing a drawdown schedule, you can, the repayment will be reduced and the remaining 7% subsidy will be released on quarterly basis.

items.statement: Receivable days currently around 60 days
items.quote: The receivable days right now, it has increased a little bit, but the average is around 60 days.

items.statement: Working capital limit Rs 80 crore sanctioned with 25% margin; comfortable for FY25 needs
items.quote: we have a working capital of ₹80 crores that was sanctioned by the bank along with 25% margin of ours. Chirag Jain: So we would be competing on that. Nasir Khan: Yes, 110 to 120. That is, I guess, we can work with that right

items.statement: Non-denim revenue target Rs 250-300 crore; balance denim for FY25
items.quote: if I talk about non-denim, non-denim will have a revenue segment of around ₹250 crores to ₹300 crores and the rest part will be denim.

items.statement: Implemented SAP S/4 HANA Cloud public version in textile composite mill
items.quote: we are the first company in India to implement SAP, SAP S/4 HANA Cloud version, public cloud version in a textile composite mill.

items.statement: Raw material price volatility and government stability cited as key risks; subsidies not factored into margin guidance
items.quote: raw material prices, we have an extreme fluctuations happening. Right now the government had become a little unstable, but it is stable, i.e. the same government will continue, so, we don't have problems in the government issues also.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth expected to be very close to double-digit
items.quote: Maybe very close to double-digit.

items.statement: Target 30-35% of business from high-margin products in next 3-4 years
items.quote: In the next 3-4 years, we target nearly 30%-35% business will be derived from high margin products.

items.statement: High-margin non-acid chloride products could lift overall EBITDA to 22-23% when they reach 30-35% of volume
items.quote: Once we are able to commercialize these products, 30%-35% of our volume should be probably EBITDA of about 22%-23%.

items.statement: New non-acid chloride products carry 15-20% higher EBITDA margin than current portfolio
items.quote: This can be almost, you can say, 15% to 20% higher than what we are earning today. In terms of the EBITDA margin, you can say.

items.statement: New acid chloride products in US and Korea have 1,000-4,000 MT/year potential each but traction will take time
items.quote: When I say good potentials these are like; 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000 metric ton a year kind of potentials. But it is going to take some time before we really, really see some major traction out of this.

items.statement: Non-acid chloride pipeline potential INR 200-250 crore when fully commercialized
items.quote: Potential of these products is quite good. It can go to INR200 crores to INR250 crores when you put all these products together.

items.statement: Greenfield capex not high on consideration; evaluating brownfield, job-work or small facility takeover with lower investment
items.quote: Probably a facility which has some possibility to just modify and then start production. Those kinds of options we are looking at. So, with little limited or lower investment, we can take less risk.

items.statement: Vizag greenfield project withdrawn due to customer growth plans halting post-COVID; no structural change in business
items.quote: Their growth plans have also kind of halted. And whatever business we had at that time or whatever business we have at this point in time, as I mentioned, there is no structural change.

items.statement: FY24 capacity utilisation 68%; targeting 78-79% in FY25
items.quote: 68% has been FY'24 and about 78%-79% we are expecting for FY'25.

items.statement: Peak revenue at full utilisation and normal pricing around INR 900-920 crore
items.quote: If we are able to utilize everything well and at whatever is the normal price that we can fetch, we can reach around INR900 crores-INR920 crores.

items.statement: Polymer volumes fell ~25% in FY24 due to customer de-stocking and cautious ordering; no structural demand loss
items.quote: Overall requirement from the customers reduced because of their end product demand being subdued, of course, on a temporary basis. As I mentioned, structure of the business has not changed.

items.statement: Aramid fibre demand growing steadily; Far East players expanding capacity, some doubling
items.quote: Some of the companies in Far East market like Korea and Japan, they are expanding their capacity for aramid fibres. Some are in fact almost doubling their capacity.

items.statement: FY24 revenue decline driven by both volume drop and price reduction as raw material costs fell 30-35% from FY23 peaks
items.quote: A couple of our raw material prices went down by almost 30%-35% than what it was in FY23.

items.statement: New products contributed ~INR 25-30 crore in FY24; 5-6 acid chlorides introduced over 3-4 years
items.quote: So, there has been contribution of about INR25 crores, INR30 crores coming from some of these new products.

items.statement: Customers ordering conservatively with back-to-back orders; no long-term contracts currently; dialogue ongoing for stable supply agreements
items.quote: Nobody is very keen to enter into something which will commit themselves for a very long time. They are just waiting and watching to see how this uncertain situation unfolds.

items.statement: Over 85% revenue from exports; freight costs rose in H2 FY24 due to Red Sea crisis but largely passed to customers
items.quote: With over 85% of our total business coming from the export market, freight and logistic costs have increased to some extent in second half due to Red Sea crisis. However, a large part of our freight cost is paid by customers.

items.statement: NSE listing application nearly ready; advisors reviewing documentation from 1970s-80s; will apply shortly
items.quote: Our advisors are examining this information and data in detail and once it is done, we will be applying to NSE very shortly.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR 14 per share (140%) for FY24
items.quote: Board has recommended a dividend of INR14, which is 140% per equity share of this value of INR10/- for the financial year 2024.

items.statement: Buyback suggestion will be placed before board; decision will balance investment needs and shareholder returns
items.quote: We will definitely put it to the board. But on one hand, you are asking me about when you are going to invest in new facilities and on the other hand, you are asking, telling me to do buyback. So, we'll have to see what is right for business.

items.statement: Silox India investment is illiquid (book value INR 309 crore, cost INR 3 crore); receiving good dividends but encashment difficult
items.quote: Valuation as per the balance sheet of that company is INR309 crores. Now, as I mentioned, that is just valuation. This is not money that we have invested. What we had invested was only INR3 crores.

items.quote: We're expecting to acquire 100% in a period of three to four years which again would be valued at 13 to 15 EBITDA multiple in the next three to four years.

items.statement: Gross written premium crossed INR 9,000 crores in FY24 with market share of 3.1% on GWP basis
items.quote: we have completed and crossed INR 9,000 crores of premium income in the last whole year. Overall market share on GWP basis is about 3.1.

items.statement: Net earned premium doubled from FY22 to FY24 reaching INR 7,000 crores
items.quote: if you look at the next line, which is the premium retention ratio, the premium retention ratio has also been increasing each year. And in FY '24, this number was about 85.8%.

items.statement: Combined ratio for FY24 was 108.7%, about 1% higher than previous year due to large property and NAT CAT losses
items.quote: Our combined ratio in FY '24 was 108.7, which is about 1% higher than the previous year. Most of it is related to some large losses in property, which we had and some NAT CAT losses.

items.statement: Profit after tax for FY24 was INR 182 crores, Q4 FY24 profit was INR 53 crores (double Q4 FY23)
items.quote: Our profit for the year is about INR 182 crores. And for the quarter, it's INR53 crores, which is double to what we had in quarter 4 of '23.

items.statement: Premium retention ratio increased to 85.8% in FY24, among highest in industry
items.quote: And in FY '24, this number was about 85.8%, which I believe would be amongst the highest in the industry.

items.statement: Own damage mix increased from 16% to 22%, TP reduced from 46% to 39%, health travel increased from 13% to 19% in FY24
items.quote: you can actually see our own damage mix has increased from 16% to 22% in FY '24. TP has actually reduced from 46% to 39%. Health travel NP has increased from 13% to 19%.

items.statement: Outgrew industry in motor OD (42% vs 17%), fire (19% vs 7%), health; de-grew motor TP by 11% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: industry has grown in motor own damage by about 17% against our 42%. TP is about 10%, which is similar to ours. Fire, industry grew by 7%, we grew by 19%. And health, etcetera, also, we grew more than the industry.

items.statement: Took corrective action in motor TP due to third-party inflation and minimum wage increases; de-grew TP by 11% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: we as a company always plan continuously look at businesses where we feel it doesn't make sense economically for us to do business. And we would actually then get out of those segments if we don't find the margins to be attractive.

items.statement: Own damage loss ratio improved year by year: 74%, 69%, 66%; TP loss ratio viewed over 3-4 year period
items.quote: if you look at our own damage loss ratios has been coming down year by year, 74, 69, 66. TP loss ratio has been coming down. But in TP loss ratio, we always look at loss ratio over a period of three years or four years

items.statement: Health loss ratio increased due to growth in employer-employee health business and lower data quality initially
items.quote: The loss ratio still was at about 72% lower than, I would say, the industry health loss ratio. And this has increased last year due to the growth in the employer -employee health insurance business.

items.statement: Property and engineering NAT CAT losses of INR 70 crores impacted combined ratio by only 1% due to high net earned premium base
items.quote: We actually had an impact of about INR70 crores, which basically meant that in case of property and engineering, this had a very, very significant impact. But what is interesting is that because we have a very high net earn ed premium of almost INR7,000 crores, the impact on the overall loss ratio for the year is only 1%.

items.statement: API integrations doubled in two years; 51% of policies now issued through APIs
items.quote: you can also see in two years, we have almost doubled the number of APIs we have. And now 51% of our policies are issued through the APIs.

items.statement: Assets under management grew organically by INR 2,700-2,800 crores in FY24; raised INR 350 crores sub-debt for solvency
items.quote: if you look at from FY23 to FY24, we have roughly increased organically the AUM by about INR2,700, INR2,800 crores. And this year we had raised INR 350 crores of sub-debt to support the solvency.

items.statement: Investment income crossed INR 1,000 crores, more than doubled from FY22; investment yield improved to 7.3% (up ~100 bps)
items.quote: The investment income is decent. We crossed INR1,000 crores in investment income. So if you actually see FY22 to FY24, our investment income has actually more than doubled. And you can also see that the investment yield is also now about 7.3%, which is almost 100 basis points better than the previous year.

items.statement: Equity allocation kept low at 1.6% due to solvency sensitivity; will increase equity allocation post IPO capital infusion
items.quote: Our equity allocation has continued to be lower. It's only 1.6%. And when we look at our solvency of 161%, since solvency ratio was a bit lower, any unrealized losses in equity passed through the solvency or passed through the P&L.

items.statement: Solvency ratio was 1.61 as of March 2024; expected to exceed 200% by June 2024 post IPO capital infusion of INR 1,125 crores
items.quote: our sense is this will be more than 200%. What exactly that number would be that we will know only on 30th of June, but we expect the solvency ratio to go beyond 200% definitely.

items.statement: Raised INR 1,125 crores through IPO; net worth increased by one-third; leverage will decrease this year then resume growth
items.quote: leverage obviously will go down this year because we have raised capital of about INR 1125 crores or so. So, our net worth will suddenly increase by one third. So, the leverage will go down.

items.statement: Reserving triangles show adequate reserving across whole account, motor TP, and non-TP lines; no negative surprises philosophy
items.quote: I think for us in Digit our philosophy, for reserving is that we need to always be adequately reserved. I think having surprises on reserving, negative surprises, is something which shouldn't really happen.

items.statement: IFRS 17 audited reconciliation published; IFRS profitability from year 3; regulator not yet mandating IFRS reporting format
items.quote: as of now the regulator is not asking us or any company to publish IFRS results. And in what shape and manner would the IFRS get implemented in India or by the regulator is something which we'll have to wait and see.

items.statement: Retail health insurance ~INR 60 crores; group health dominates portfolio; health business under industry stress due to portability and waiting period dynamics
items.quote: most of our portfolio would be gro up. And retail health insurance would be a smaller number. If I remember offhand, this would be close to about INR60 crores or so for last year

items.statement: Support motor TP de-tariffing; industry priority is TP rate increase (no increase in 4 years); free pricing would shift competition from commission to price
items.quote: our view is that sooner or later, one should have de -tariffing simply because this is the only segment where there is no free pricing. Secondly, when the pricing is fixed, then people play on the commission, on the acquisition cost.

items.statement: Channel agnostic strategy; broker channel includes OEM, corporate, retail, aggregators - all with different loss ratios and acquisition costs
items.quote: we as a company are channel agnostic which basically means that we try and steer business through all possible distribution channels, looking at their own each channels, own loss ratio as well as acquisition cost.

items.statement: No target channel or product mix; market dynamics change rapidly (e.g., OEM channel fluctuates with auto sales cycles)
items.quote: there is no real channel mix which we steer towards to say in 2 years this is the channel mix which we want. Because I think again, based on our understanding of business market changes very fast.

items.statement: B2B strategy (fire, engineering, group health) combines relationships, underwriting expertise, reinsurance capacity, and claims settlement ability; earned right to win daily
items.quote: it actually becomes a mix of all of this. As far as I think right to etc etera goes, as you rightly said, we are a small player in this. But despite that, we did INR800 crores of property premium last year.

items.statement: No guidance on combined ratio trajectory; business driven by profitability not growth targets; will de-grow unprofitable segments
items.quote: we don't really -- we are not really in a position to give any guidance and nor we want to give guidance because we don't drive our business from that perspective.

items.statement: NAT CAT losses unpredictable; expect 1/3 to 1/2 of FY24 losses annually but not uniformly distributed; impact limited by growing premium base
items.quote: One would expect, I would say, half of these losses or one third of these losses to come every year. But the losses will never, ever be uniformly distributed.

items.statement: Motor TP de-growth in Q4 FY24 driven by commercial vehicles (90% TP premium); will re-enter when market corrects
items.quote: if we de-gr ew in motor third -party, you can be sure that the de -growth would have happened more because of commercial vehicles, because commercial vehicles have almost 90% of the premium coming in from third-party.

items.statement: Targeting 15% ROCE from FY27 at 80% capacity utilization
items.quote: we are targeting to achieve a ratio of almost 15%, and that we should start looking at from when we hit the capacity of, say, 80%, which we are targeting by, say, third year. So, one can safely assume that from '27, that is the return which we are looking at.

items.statement: INR 3,000 crores milestone payments for Krishnapatnam and Jodhpur completion
items.quote: out of which we will be releasing milestone payments of almost INR3,000 crores. This is the completion of Krishnapatnam as well as completion of the Marwar Jodhpur unit

items.quote: end of this year we should be hitting almost like operating capacity of say, 96 million tons and by FY26, I should be giving good news of 110 million tons.

items.quote: I would say about INR300 per ton cost efficiency is something very doable. And on the pricing side as you know Ambuja ACC are A category price players. So there is always a INR5 to INR10 upside on the pricing.

items.quote: this number will go to INR1500, INR1000. See what we are doing at Ambuja, ACC level we are running on a cost on margin optimization program of INR550 which we had also announced in the last earnings call.

items.statement: Will apply Ambuja/ACC playbook: base brand, two premium brands, OPC and blended for B2B
items.quote: we have a very good playbook for our brands, for Ambuja and ACC. We have typically a base brand and we have two premium brands for each of the company which is the playbook we have for Pan India.

items.statement: South India demand growth expected with new AP regime; industry consolidation improving pricing discipline
items.quote: Mind you, there will be a substantial growth in large parts of the country, especially with the new regime in place in AP. I believe there should be a lot of development work. So some demand will happen there.

items.quote: whatever is the pending parcels of land which will be required for the railway line and for the limestone reserves in due course, they are acquiring it. And that will be part of the overall enterprise value.

items.statement: Jodhpur 3 MTPA kiln and Krishnapatnam 2 MTPA grinding unit completion in 12 and 9 months respectively
items.quote: For Krishnapatnam, we are giving a timeline of say, nine months and Rajasthan, 12 months. Yes.

items.statement: 140 MTPA target by March 2028 on track; 20 MTPA under commissioning, 30 MTPA blueprint ready with land and mining
items.quote: we are well poised to hit our 140 million ton target, as we have been speaking in past.

items.quote: On top of this cement capacity, we have five bulk cement terminals and one 25,500 tons self -discharging cement carrier, which will beautifully complement our coastal logistics strategy.

items.statement: INR 5-10/ton pricing upside as A-category player; INR 300/ton cost reduction from AFR, RE, group synergies
items.quote: on the pricing side as you know Ambuja ACC are A category price players. So there is always a INR5 to INR10 upside on the pricing. So if I put INR10 on pricing and INR300 on cost we are talking about INR500 EBITDA kick up from the current levels

items.quote: The entire acquisition will be funded through cash and cash equivalents. After all of this also, by end of this year, my estimate is that we will be holding almost INR10,000 plus crores of cash.

items.quote: When I look at Penna, in 2022, Penna itself did about 6.5 million, 6.6 million. So that plus what we are doing, and we have taken a very considered ramp-up plan.

items.quote: So, we are expecting that at least for the next 2-3 quarters, this is going to continue and I think as I mentioned that any increase in freight rates definitely also helps us improve our margins as well.

items.quote: I would say it will idea is that since we are in the cost-plus model, you know we will have to pass on this increase to our customer. items.statement: Business shifting from China to India and Vietnam will grow Indian international trade and benefit Tiger Logistics
items.quote: So, at the moment whatever is getting banned, it's getting transferred either to India or to Vietnam or to other countries. So definitely the Indian international business is going to grow and that benefit will definitely come on to us.

items.statement: Import volume mix growing from 15% currently, targeting higher share to reduce export dependence
items.quote: I think it is only increasing. We are looking at imports also contributing pretty well in the coming quarters. So that ratio is increasing. We don't want to be purely dependent on exports.

items.statement: Shanghai-Chennai 40ft container rate surged from $800 in Feb-Mar 2024 to $4,500 currently
items.quote: I tell you in the in the month of February'24 and March'24, the 120 feet container from Shanghai to Chennai was around $800 and same container today is at $4,500, 40 feet container.

items.statement: Launched FreightJar 2.0 with global access, real-time rates, better customer experience; hiring for this vertical
items.quote: we were able to finalize the Version 2 of our logistics online platform Freight Jar which will definitely give us better access to more markets and better access to more customers & clients who are dealing in the international business.

items.statement: Won government contracts including 1-year HPCL petrochemical logistics and BHEL ODC/container shipments
items.quote: Development of the government projects business, it's doing well for us. We've got some good contracts this quarter as well.

items.quote: The revenue model is purely what we are doing now. Since it is a sales product of Tiger Logistics, we are offering the same services through the online portal. So, the margin remains the same at 7%-8% whatever is there in our business.

items.quote: the only thing which is lacking is that we were looking at some kind of inorganic growth in terms of acquiring LCL company, which has not happened because you know we were not able to get the company which is aligned to our idea of growth.

items.statement: Robust order book exceeding INR 40 crores

items.statement: Targeting sustainable 25-30% year-on-year growth
items.quote: So I think we will be able to achieve a very sustainable growth of 25%, 30% year-on-year. So that is also our target to be sustainable.

items.quote: Present we have around 15 CR CapEx. So we are planning yeah. Yeah. We are planning to have some more machineries, technological machine s and equipment in future so we can enhance our productivity also with the new technologies we will have increase in the ROCE

items.quote: So, yeah. I can say if you just put it in numbers literally, it will be 30%, 40% increase.

items.quote: It is possible that the foundry will add to somewhere shares increase the margin, I think, by 3%. It is possible. Yes.

items.statement: 50-60% of revenues expected from defense sector
items.quote: 50-60% revenues will come only from defense.

items.statement: Huge surge in domestic shipbuilding and naval projects; capacity utilization was 100% for domestic demand
items.quote: Even in the coming future, we see a huge demand from the Indian local PSUs with the defense maritime, marine and as the things are progressing, we see that there is a huge surge in the local domestic shipbuilding projects, naval projects, where we have to also significantly gear up.

items.statement: H2O Dynamics water treatment venture receiving 20-25 inquiries, expecting conversion
items.quote: What I want to add that we just started, but the response from the industry is very much overwhelming, like we are getting we almost got 20, 25 inquiries right now. And most of the inquiries we are seeing that we can convert into the business.

items.statement: German filter technology for automatic cleaning; 80% Make in India, 20% parts from Germany
items.quote: Make in India. And some parts, say, around 20% parts will come from Germany, 80% of it will be made in India.

items.statement: Seasonality trend H1/H2 30-70% or 40-60% to continue for couple of years due to consolidation
items.quote: So it always it will be a trend for at least a couple of years. Once you are at a particular level, once your things are great, things are in auto mode, then this trend start, this trend becomes both the quarters become try to equalize.

items.statement: Projects FY25 fertilizer sales volume of 25 lakh tons, a 25% rise over expected FY24 volumes

items.statement: Expects FY24 fertilizer volume growth of 10% to reach around 20 lakh metric tons
items.quote: But overall year, we will be clocking the 10% volume growth in fertilizer business. So we will be reaching around 20 lakh metric tons for the year.

items.statement: Projects FY24 turnover around INR9,000 crores
items.quote: We are expected to clock around INR9,000 crores turnover this year.

items.statement: Q3 fertilizer margins under pressure due to subsidy reduction from October 2023 while input costs increased

items.statement: Some relief in Q4 fertilizer operations expected due to lower phosphoric acid and ammonia prices
items.quote: So some relief in Q4 fertilizer operations may be there. On subsidy, government has already provided for the supplementary budget of INR13,000 crores.

items.quote: So we'll be having the sulphuric acid plant of 1,800 metric tons per day at Sikka. That sulphuric acid will be used as a NPK and this APS fertilizer.

items.quote: Like 600 metric tons per day, 2 lakh metric tons per year phos acid plant. So that will help in making DAP and NPK fertilizer in Sikka.

items.statement: Current urea plant energy consumption at 6.5 Gcal/ton, government mandating 6.2 Gcal/ton
items.quote: Right now, it is around 6.5 Gcal per ton. And government is now insisting for 6.2 Gcal per ton.

items.statement: Natural gas requirement 16-18 lakh tons daily, 70-75% for fertilizers, balance for chemicals
items.value: 16 lakh tons to 18 lakh tons of gas daily
items.quote: So broadly, we require around 16 lakh tons to 18 lakh tons of gas daily a sub-tube of gas. And about 70%, 75% is used for fertilizers. Balance is used for chemicals.

items.statement: Average gas cost in Q3 broadly INR45-50 per SM3, stable versus Q2
items.quote: So broadly INR45 to INR50 per SM3. That is the Q3 versus Q2 price difference. This year, gas prices are fairly stable.

items.value: $17 and ammonia prices which were more than $500 are now less than $400
items.quote: Phosphoric acid has come down by $17 and ammonia prices which were more than $500 are now less than $400.

items.statement: Government reduced P&K subsidies 30-50% from October 2023 while keeping MRP stable for farmers
items.quote: The subsidy deduction were anywhere from 30% to more than 50% in different products. So that is why the -- it is showing up like this.

items.statement: New P&K reasonability notification allows 12% margin over cost of production, excludes GST from revenue
items.quote: So government has clarified that 12% margin over cost of production will be taken as reasonable margin and beyond which it will be considered as unreasonable and maybe mocked up.

items.quote: So we sell from 30,000, 35,000 tons of TGU every year. And just like a normal chemical, it is sold between -- at full cost between INR35,000 to INR40,000 per ton.

items.statement: Urea energy norms savings pass to government, not retained by company unless exceeding norms
items.quote: So even when the companies are reducing the Gcal for Gcal consumption of energy, that saving is taken over by the government. It is not kept with the company.

items.statement: Ammonium sulphate subsidy based on imported urea cost, not linked to domestic natural gas prices
items.quote: Government won't take into account natural gas price for N. They look at urea -- imported urea cost to the country. And from there, they derive N.

items.statement: Inventory increased INR92 crores in Q3 due to off-season, no advance billing
items.quote: Yes, because this is off season. So we don't do any advanced billing, we do whatever is required by the field. So there will be some inventory during this quarter.

items.statement: Company is debt-free with healthy cash flows, subsidy received regularly up to January for urea and December for P&K
items.quote: As you all know, we are a debt-free company, and we have a good amount of liquid cash in our hand.

items.statement: Dividend expected INR10 or more for FY24 based on 30% of profit or 5% of net worth guideline
items.quote: So I think INR10 or more dividend can be expected this year.

items.quote: That Board of Directors will take a call at suitable time.

items.statement: Wage revision from January 1, 2023 incorporated in employee costs, will stabilize by March 2024
items.quote: Last time wage revision has been done from 01/01/23. So that provision has been incorporated in the employee numbers. So till March '24 that will keep showing rise and it will stabilize.

items.statement: No visibility on government increasing fertilizer subsidy from January 2024, likely only from April
items.quote: Government is quick in reducing the subsidy but increasing it is difficult. So more or less, it will be from April onwards only.

items.statement: Expects 15-20% growth in fertilizer sales volume for FY24 vs FY23
items.quote: As I said in the morning, we are expecting 15% to 20% rise in volume in fertilizer sales this year.

items.statement: Targets FY24 revenue similar to FY23 level of INR11,368 crore
items.quote: On overall basis, we expect that we will maintain this turnover, last year turnover in this year also.

items.statement: Expects dividend income of INR140 crore in FY24 from investee companies
items.quote: No, it will be much more. It will be INR140 crores.

items.statement: Plans INR4,000 crore investment over two years for chemical business at Dahej
items.quote: So right now we are receiving a further investment of INR4,000 crores in the head for chemical business.

items.quote: So in this August, we have crossed last year's June production and we hope to reach our install capacity of 7,22,000 tons, that is 100% production of install capacity and that is our target this year.

items.statement: Ammonia project commissioning by December 2023; other projects on schedule
items.quote: We will be commissioning ammonia for project by December 23, and other projects will be coming up as per the timeline mentioned.

items.statement: Sikka unit produced 2.73 lakh tons in FY23; crossed 2 lakh tons by July FY24
items.quote: This production, all the products together were 2,73,000 tons. So up to July, we have crossed 2 lakh tons.

items.statement: Q1 FY24 impacted by INR120-125 crore one-time subsidy and inventory write-downs
items.quote: So in all, around INR120 crores INR125 crores could be said to be one time effect, not really pertaining to this quarter.

items.statement: Industrial product margins improving from July; full impact visible in H2 FY24
items.quote: But as I said, full impact will be seen in H2. It is improving in this quarter. But not so much.

items.statement: Gas prices down >25% vs Q1 FY23; now stable
items.quote: It is reduced compared to, say, Q1 last year, it is more than 25% reduction. But as of now, it is stable kind of thing.

items.quote: Base quarter's price is expected to be around $850, July to September. October onwards still prices are not decided. So this quarter, like last year, I mean October to December it was $1,700, now it has halved to $850, it is half now.

items.quote: It is DAP, then ammonium phosphate sulphate APS, then NPK 10 and NPK 12, four products.

items.quote: We have a good brand recall amongst the farmers, so selling is not a problem. And we, depending on the requirement, we cater to the whole country, so our market is quite wide.

items.quote: And we also hope that looking to the economic scenario, government will calibrate the subsidy from October considering all the relevant factors and so much reduction in subsidy may or may not take place.

items.quote: So as I said, the buyback bonus and splitting of shares, all those proposals will be examined by the GSFC Board and whatever outcome or decision is that will be announced whenever it is decided some concrete course of action.

items.quote: During 2025, we expect both entities to generate INR600 crores to INR650 crores of revenue and a PAT of INR15 crores to INR17 crores.

items.quote: We are looking to achieve INR6,000 crores revenue, 3% to 4% PAT margin and of 25% ROCE.
